01@Rodentologist.text: The condition is ``Birds that eat [rodent]'', not ``Birds that only eat [rodent]'', and the clarification text is ``Any bird with a [rodent] symbol. The bird may also eat other kinds of food.'' (These misprints were corrected in the third printing, and a corrected card is available in the update pack.)

20220213@Rodentologist.text: Only birds showing the [rodent] symbol in their printed food cost count; a [wild] (any food) symbol, e.g. \textbf{American Crow}, does not count.
20220213@Rodentologist.author: Joe Aubrey

02a@Bewick's Wren.text: When using this bird's power to move this bird to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.

20250319@Blue Grosbeak.text: \textbf{Common Myna}'s habitat restriction applies only to where it can be played, not to where it can move, so if it copies \textbf{Blue Grosbeak}'s power it may move out of the [grassland].
20250319@Blue Grosbeak.author: Joe Aubrey

02a@Blue Grosbeak.text: When using this bird's power to move it to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.

20200528@Blue Grosbeak.text: Both ``beak'' and ``head'' are on the \textbf{Anatomist} list, so birds such as \textbf{Blue Grosbeak} and \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike} count. ``Horn'' is not on the list, so \textbf{Horned Lark} does not count; follow the printed list strictly, including the additions in the expansion rulebooks.
20200528@Blue Grosbeak.author: Joe Aubrey

20221228@Blue Grosbeak.text: \textbf{Blue Grosbeak}'s power may be used every time it is activated, as long as no other bird in its habitat is to its right; it may be moved again to a different habitat on a later turn.
20221228@Blue Grosbeak.author: Jamey Stegmaier

02a@Chimney Swift.text: When using this bird's power to move this bird to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.

02a@Common Nighthawk.text: When using this bird's power to move this bird to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.

02a@Lincoln's Sparrow.text: When using this bird's power to move this bird to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.

20220521a@Song Sparrow.text: This bird may move from any column, including the leftmost one, as long as there are no birds to the right of it in its row (Appendix, page 12).
20220521a@Song Sparrow.author: Jamey Stegmaier

02a@Song Sparrow.text: When using this bird's power to move it to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.

20191007@Song Sparrow.text: For the \textbf{food cost of played birds} end-of-round goal, the clarification to count only 1 food for birds with a choice in their food cost refers to the ``/'' in food costs. \textbf{Song Sparrow} ([invertebrate]/[seed]/[fruit]) counts as 1, while \textbf{Fish Crow} ([fish]+[wild]) counts as 2.
20191007@Song Sparrow.author: Jamey Stegmaier

02a@White-Crowned Sparrow.text: When using this bird's power to move this bird to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.

02a@Yellow-Breasted Chat.text: When using this bird's power to move this bird to another habitat, the action cube does not change habitats with it.

02b@Omnivore Specialist.text: The percentage on this bonus card should be 16\%. (This misprint was corrected in print by February 2020.)

02c@Prairie.text: The word \textit{prairie} is a keyword for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card. (This omission was corrected in print by December 2019.)

20200331@Cartographer.text: ``Turkey'' does not count as a geography term for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, and neither does ``turkey vulture'' (turkey vultures are named after the bird, not the country).
20200331@Cartographer.author: Joe Aubrey

20240526@Cartographer.text: ``Wood'' (singular) in a bird's name is not a geography term for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, so birds such as \textbf{Wood Stork} and woodswallows do not count.
20240526@Cartographer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20241104@Cartographer.text: \textbf{Red Junglefowl} counts toward the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, since ``jungle'' appears in its name.
20241104@Cartographer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

02c@Cartographer.text: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, including \textit{prairie} (which is printed on this bonus card only in newer printings), and those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks.

20201230a@Cartographer.text: \textbf{Cartographer} awards a flat bonus for the tier reached, not points per qualifying bird: at least 2 qualifying birds scores 3 points, at least 4 scores 7 points.
20201230a@Cartographer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200229@Cartographer.text: On this bonus card ``name'' refers only to the common name, not the scientific name.

02d@Greater Prairie-Chicken.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card: \textit{prairie} is a qualifying keyword. (Early printings of that bonus card did not list it; the omission was corrected in print by December 2019.)

02e@Photographer.text: The 3-point bonus applies when there are 4--5 qualifying birds on your player mat, not 2--3. (This misprint was corrected in the third printing, and a corrected card is available in the update pack.)

20230529@Photographer.text: \textbf{Baya Weaver} does not count toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card. That card looks for colors as words or as part of compound words, and ``Baya'' is its own word, not a compound of ``bay'' and ``a''.
20230529@Photographer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210401@Photographer.text: \textit{Rainbow} is not a color and does not count toward this bonus card.
20210401@Photographer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220521@Photographer.text: \textit{Redstart} and \textit{yellowthroat} both count toward this bonus card; a full list of qualifying colors appears on page 4 of the Appendix.
20220521@Photographer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191203b@Photographer.text: The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks (excluding \textit{honey}, which the \textit{European Expansion} rulebook listed but which stopped being a keyword when the Oceania Expansion was released), and \textit{violet}, which appears on \textbf{Violet Cuckoo} and \textbf{Violet-Green Swallow}. Substrings of bird names that coincide with color names do not count toward this bonus when not referring to colors (e.g., the \textit{red} in \textbf{Barred Owl}), but see \textbf{Northern Bobwhite}.

20220610@Photographer.text: The point values on this bonus card are totals, not per-bird: if you have the number of qualifying birds shown, you gain that number of points in total.
20220610@Photographer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200229@Photographer.text: On this bonus card ``name'' refers only to the common name, not the scientific name.

02f@Spotted Sandpiper.text: This bird is worth 5 points, not 4. (This misprint was corrected in the third printing, and a corrected card is available in the update pack.)

02g@Rerolling dice.text: Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder: whenever you go to the birdfeeder to gain food for any reason---caching included, and including a power that gains 1 [die] or that gains a specific food ``if available''---you may reroll if all the [die] in the birdfeeder show the same face. A single remaining [die] trivially shows the same face, so it may be rerolled. You may also take fewer food than the birdfeeder offers and reroll before choosing the next.

03a@Powers.text: "Only powers of birds played on a player mat can be used. In particular, birds with the power ``This bird counts double toward the end-of-round goal, if it qualifies for the goal."" (e.g., \textbf{Cetti's Warbler}) does not count double toward the \textbf{[card] in hand} end-of-round goal."

20230827a@Common Blackbird.text: Although \textbf{Common Blackbird} is placed sideways and covers 2 [forest] spaces, playing it still only allows you to place 1 duet token on the duet map.
20230827a@Common Blackbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

03b@Common Blackbird.text: If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.

20201104@Common Blackbird.text: The \textbf{white \& no powers} end-of-round goal counts both birds with ``when played'' powers (white cards, e.g. \textbf{Common Blackbird}) and birds with no powers at all (e.g. \textbf{American Woodcock}, \textbf{Wild Turkey}).
20201104@Common Blackbird.author: Joe Aubrey

20201104b@Common Blackbird.text: Although \textbf{Common Blackbird} is placed sideways across 2 [forest] spaces, it still counts as only 1 bird whenever birds in a habitat are counted, such as for an end-of-round goal.
20201104b@Common Blackbird.author: Joe Aubrey

20200405@Common Buzzard.text: \textbf{Common Buzzard} counts toward the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

03b@Common Buzzard.text: If \textbf{Common Buzzard} is played on top of a horizontal bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.

2020022b@Common Buzzard.text: In games where the Automa has drawn the \textbf{Citizen Scientist} bonus card, this bird qualifies for that bonus card.

20200405@Eurasian Hobby.text: \textbf{Eurasian Hobby} counts toward the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

03b@Eurasian Hobby.text: If \textbf{Eurasian Hobby} is played on top of a horizontal bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.

2020022b@Eurasian Hobby.text: In games where the Automa has drawn the \textbf{Citizen Scientist} bonus card, this bird qualifies for that bonus card.

03b@European Roller.text: If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.

03b@Grey Heron.text: If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of \textbf{Grey Heron}, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.

20220830@Grey Heron.text: \textbf{Grey Heron} fills two [wetland] spaces and helps fill two columns, but it still counts as only a single bird (e.g., for the \textbf{birds in one row} end-of-round goal) and counts once toward goals and scoring that count birds in a habitat.
20220830@Grey Heron.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201011@Long-Tailed Tit.text: When scoring the \textbf{Site Selection Expert} bonus card, \textbf{Long-Tailed Tit}'s [star] nest can count as a different nest type in each of the two columns it occupies.

03b@Long-Tailed Tit.text: If a bird (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) is played on top of this one, the top bird is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.

03c@Montagu's Harrier.text: Even when using this bird's power to play it on top of another bird, this bird may only be played in [grassland].

03b@Montagu's Harrier.text: If this bird is played on top of a horizontal one (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.

20200405@Montagu's Harrier.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

2020022b@Montagu's Harrier.text: In games where the Automa has drawn the \textbf{Citizen Scientist} bonus card, this bird qualifies for that bonus card.

20260324@Red Kite.text: With \textbf{Garden Warbler}, the additional bird is played first and completely, including its own ``when played'' power, and only then is 1 [egg] laid on both birds. If the additional bird is \textbf{Red Kite} (or a similar bird) played on top of \textbf{Garden Warbler}, turning \textbf{Garden Warbler} into a tucked card, the egg laying still takes place.
20260324@Red Kite.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240714a@Red Kite.text: Playing \textbf{Red Kite} on top of another bird in a player's [grassland] still counts as playing a bird in that habitat, so it triggers \textbf{Horned Lark}.
20240714a@Red Kite.author: Jamey Stegmaier

03b@Red Kite.text: If this bird is played on top of a horizontal one (e.g., \textbf{Common Blackbird}), it is also placed horizontally and occupies both columns.

20200405@Red Kite.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

2020022b@Red Kite.text: In games where the Automa has drawn the \textbf{Citizen Scientist} bonus card, this bird qualifies for that bonus card.

20190117@Great Crested Flycatcher.text: When using this bird's power, if all [die] in the birdfeeder show the same face you may reroll before taking food.
20190117@Great Crested Flycatcher.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190122@Sets of [egg][egg][egg] in [for.text: A player's score for this goal tile is the minimum of the counts of eggs in each of their habitats.

20210199a@Gray Catbird.text: When \textbf{Gray Catbird} repeats the power of a bird with a ``copy'' power (e.g., the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}), it repeats the copying power printed on that bird and not any powers that bird copied earlier in the turn.

20190127@Gray Catbird.text: \textbf{Gray Catbird} may repeat the brown power of any bird in the habitat, whether it is to the left or right.

20210199a@Hooded Merganser.text: \textbf{Hooded Merganser} cannot copy the power of a bird with a ``copy'' power that is not a predator power, even if that bird copied a predator power earlier in the turn.

20220307@Hooded Merganser.text: When a bird power refers to a characteristic of other birds, only birds currently on your player mat are applicable, not birds in your hand or elsewhere, unless the power specifically says otherwise (such as a power that looks at the top card of the deck). \textbf{Hooded Merganser} therefore repeats the power of a bird with the [predator] icon already played in its habitat, and a bird whose power it repeats may also be activated in its own right during the same turn as the action cube moves along the row.
20220307@Hooded Merganser.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190127@Hooded Merganser.text: \textbf{Hooded Merganser} activates another bird's brown power, and it may activate a bird's power regardless of whether that bird is to the left or right of it.

20260111@Hooded Merganser.text: \textbf{Hooded Merganser}'s power is activated as a brown power, so it can only repeat another brown power -- specifically a [predator] power -- and the repeated bird must be in the same habitat.

20240110@Northern Mockingbird.text: Copy powers act as if the copied text were printed on the copying bird. So if \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} copies the \textbf{Northern Mockingbird}'s power, you then repeat a brown power on another bird in \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}'s own habitat ([forest]).
20240110@Northern Mockingbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210199a@Northern Mockingbird.text: When \textbf{Northern Mockingbird} repeats the power of a bird with a ``copy'' power (e.g., the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}), it repeats the copying power printed on that bird and not any powers that bird copied earlier in the turn.

20190127@Northern Mockingbird.text: \textbf{Northern Mockingbird} may repeat the brown power of any bird in the habitat, whether it is to the left or right.

20190309@House Wren.text: If you use \textbf{House Wren}'s power to play another bird with a ``play a second bird'' power, you may then use the latter bird's power to play yet another bird. Pay each bird's printed food cost and the [egg] cost at the top of the column it is placed in.
20190309@House Wren.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190128@House Wren.text: The additional bird must be played in the same habitat as \textbf{House Wren}. Because the power says a ``second'' bird, it looks at the first bird, so even though \textbf{House Wren} itself may be played in either of two habitats, both birds go in the same one.
20190128@House Wren.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190203@Brewer's Blackbird.text: If this bird already has the maximum number of [egg] on it, you may still use its power to tuck a [card]; you simply cannot lay the [egg].

20190203@Bushtit.text: If this bird already has the maximum number of [egg] on it, you may still use its power to tuck a [card]; you simply cannot lay the [egg].

20231204@Common Grackle.text: A [card] drawn with \textbf{Wilson's Storm Petrel} or \textbf{Great Crested Grebe} may not be tucked with \textbf{Common Grackle}. Those [card] are kept separate from your hand and cannot be spent during the turn in which they were drawn (Appendix).
20231204@Common Grackle.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201230@Ruby-Crowned Kinglet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260128@Tufted Titmouse.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200617@American Oystercatcher.text: You may take the drawn cards from the deck and/or from the bird tray, despite this bird's entry in the Appendix.

20201010@American Oystercatcher.text: You must draw all X+1 cards as instructed, since some of them are allocated to other players.

20250603@American Oystercatcher.text: The drawn cards are revealed: players look at them before choosing, rather than selecting blind.
20250603@American Oystercatcher.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221123@American Oystercatcher.text: Unless a power specifies that cards must be drawn from the deck or from the bird tray, you may choose where to draw each [card] from: the face-up cards in the bird tray or the top of the deck. On \textbf{Indian Peafowl}, the additional [card] you draw may come from either source, even though the first 2 [card] must come from the deck.
20221123@American Oystercatcher.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190311@American Oystercatcher.text: In a game against the Automa, draw 3 [card] and keep 2; the Automa is not passed a [card], so the third is discarded.
20190311@American Oystercatcher.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190313@Once between turns.text: You may activate each ``once between turns'' power on a bird on your player mat once between each of your turns.

20220515@Lazuli Bunting.text: A power may be activated even if its full benefit is not possible; as much of it as possible is implemented. For example, \textbf{Lazuli Bunting}'s power may be used even if another player has no [bowl] bird with an empty nest to lay an [egg] on.
20220515@Lazuli Bunting.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190406@Lazuli Bunting.text: If you use \textbf{Lazuli Bunting}'s power to lay 2 [egg], they must be laid on different [bowl]/[star] birds.

20240604@Pileated Woodpecker.text: When \textbf{Pileated Woodpecker}'s power is activated, other players may choose not to lay an [egg].
20240604@Pileated Woodpecker.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231126@Pileated Woodpecker.text: ``May'' indicates a binary option: you may do exactly as instructed, or you may not do it at all. It never licenses substituting a different action. On \textbf{Blue Jay}, you may cache the gained [seed] on this bird or keep it in your personal supply, since you have already gained it. On \textbf{Pileated Woodpecker}, you may lay the additional [egg] on a [cavity] bird or lay no additional [egg] at all.
20231126@Pileated Woodpecker.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190406@Pileated Woodpecker.text: If you use \textbf{Pileated Woodpecker}'s power to lay 2 [egg], they must be laid on different [cavity]/[star] birds.

20190406@Western Meadowlark.text: If you use this bird's power to lay 2 [egg], they must be laid on different [ground]/[star] birds.

20190522@Burrowing Owl.text: This bird does not count toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card.

20190601@Rerolling dice.text: You may only reroll dice when gaining food from the birdfeeder and not when gaining food from the supply.

20230110@Anatomist.text: The \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card was reprinted in the Asia expansion with 6 points instead of 7 for 4+ birds. The change was unintentional, but the most recent version of the card is the official one.
20230110@Anatomist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190724@Anatomist.text: Only the keywords listed on the card and in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks qualify a bird. Substrings that coincide with body-part names do not count when they do not refer to a body part (e.g., the \textit{wing} in \textbf{Burrowing Owl}).

20200528@Anatomist.text: Both ``beak'' and ``head'' are on the \textbf{Anatomist} list, so birds such as \textbf{Blue Grosbeak} and \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike} count. ``Horn'' is not on the list, so \textbf{Horned Lark} does not count; follow the printed list strictly, including the additions in the expansion rulebooks.
20200528@Anatomist.author: Joe Aubrey

20201116@Anatomist.text: \textit{Back} is a body part for this bonus card, as listed in the \textit{European Expansion} rulebook (``Anatomist (birds with body parts in their names): back, leg, toe''), so \textbf{Canvasback} counts toward it.
20201116@Anatomist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240909@Anatomist.text: \textbf{Desert Wheatear} counts toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card (``ear'').
20240909@Anatomist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200229@Anatomist.text: On this bonus card ``name'' refers only to the common name, not the scientific name.

20190724@Barred Owl.text: This bird does not count toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.
20190724@Barred Owl.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200109b@Barrow's Goldeneye.text: You may not use this bird's power to lay an [egg] on another player's bird.

20190921@Barrow's Goldeneye.text: A bird with a [star] nest counts as any and all nest types at all times throughout the game, including for egg-laying powers, bonus cards, and end-of-round goals. A power such as \textbf{Barrow's Goldeneye}'s that lays 1 [egg] on a bird with a [cavity] nest may lay it on a bird with a [star] nest.
20190921@Barrow's Goldeneye.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190729@Barrow's Goldeneye.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.

20250312@Common Goldeneye.text: For \textbf{Common Goldeneye}, birds with a [star] (wild) nest count as birds with a [cavity] nest.
20250312@Common Goldeneye.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190729@Common Goldeneye.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.

20190729@Eurasian Golden Oriole.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.

20220307@Golden Eagle.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200907@Golden Eagle.text: When paying a bird's food cost, you may exchange any 2 food tokens to stand in for 1 food of any type you lack. 20190729@Golden Eagle.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.

20190908@End of your turn.text: You may perform an action even if it precludes you from performing an action required at the end of your turn (e.g., discarding a [card] from your hand at the end of a turn in which you activated the \textbf{Black Tern}'s power).

20191010@End of your turn.text: If you perform more than one action ``at the end of your turn'', you may perform those actions in any order.

20220211@Snow Bunting.text: \textbf{Snow Bunting}'s power does not trigger during your own turn: if another player's ``once between turns'' power causes them to tuck a [card] while it is still your turn, it is not between your turns and \textbf{Snow Bunting} does not activate.
20220211@Snow Bunting.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220916@Snow Bunting.text: \textbf{Snow Bunting}'s power uses ``then,'' so you must tuck a [card] from your hand to gain the ``draw 1 [card]'' benefit.
20220916@Snow Bunting.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191229@Snow Bunting.text: Draw the [card] from the bird tray before it is refilled.

20200405@Snow Bunting.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Bird Counter} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

20191126a@Snow Bunting.text: \textbf{Snow Bunting} counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card, since \textit{snowy} is a qualifying keyword.
20191126a@Snow Bunting.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191126b@American Redstart.text: This bird's power lets you take 1 food from the birdfeeder, as if [wild] were replaced by [die] in the power text.

20191207@American Redstart.text: This bird does not count toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card.

20191127@Greater Flamingo.text: This bird's power is brown despite its entry in the \textit{European Expansion} rulebook appendix.

20200204@Greater Flamingo.text: Since this power is brown, when activating it in a game against the Automa the Automa always has zero action cubes in its [wetland].

20191202@End-of-round goal.text: A card in your hand with the power, ``This bird counts double toward the end-of-round goal, if it qualifies for the goal.'' (e.g., \textbf{Cetti's Warbler}), does not count toward end-of-round goals.

20191201@Northern Bobwhite.text: The ``white'' in \textbf{Northern Bobwhite} counts as a color for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.
20191201@Northern Bobwhite.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191203c@Violet.text: The word \textit{violet} is a keyword for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card. (This keyword currently occurs only on the \textbf{Violet-Green Swallow}, which already contains another keyword for \textbf{Photographer}.)

20191204@Moltoni's Warbler.text: If you use this bird's power to play another bird with a teal power, you may resolve that power at any point among your other remaining teal powers.

20260510@White Wagtail.text: Which action types you used this round is read from where each action cube ended up. A bird such as \textbf{Lineated Woodpecker} that moves with the action cube to another habitat therefore changes which action the cube records.
20260510@White Wagtail.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191204@White Wagtail.text: If you use \textbf{White Wagtail}'s power to play another bird with a teal power, you may resolve that power at any point among your other remaining teal powers.

20230910@Yellowhammer.text: If you use \textbf{Yellowhammer}'s power to play a bird with a round-end (teal) power, you may activate that newly played bird's power at any point among your other remaining teal powers, as long as you are still in the round-end power activation step.
20230910@Yellowhammer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201203@Black Redstart.text: You may take less of the benefit: lay [egg] on only some of the birds in the chosen habitat rather than all of them.
20201203@Black Redstart.author: Joe Aubrey

20201203@Lesser Whitethroat.text: You may take less of the benefit: lay [egg] on only some of the birds in the chosen habitat rather than all of them.
20201203@Lesser Whitethroat.author: Joe Aubrey

20191207@Black Redstart.text: This bird does not count toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card.

20191207@Painted Whitestart.text: This bird does not count toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card.

20200109b@American Avocet.text: You may not use this bird's power to lay an [egg] on another player's bird.

20190921@American Avocet.text: A bird with a [star] nest counts as any and all nest types at all times throughout the game, including for egg-laying powers, bonus cards, and end-of-round goals. A power such as \textbf{American Avocet}'s that lays 1 [egg] on a bird with a [ground] nest may lay it on a bird with a [star] nest.
20190921@American Avocet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190718@Bronzed Cowbird.text: \textbf{Bronzed Cowbird} has an egg limit of 0 and cannot hold eggs.
20190718@Bronzed Cowbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200109b@Bronzed Cowbird.text: You may not use this bird's power to lay an [egg] on another player's bird.

20190921@Bronzed Cowbird.text: A bird with a [star] nest counts as any and all nest types at all times throughout the game, including for egg-laying powers, bonus cards, and end-of-round goals. 20190921@Bronzed Cowbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200109b@Brown-Headed Cowbird.text: You may not use this bird's power to lay an [egg] on another player's bird.

20200323@Brown-Headed Cowbird.text: Eggs laid by any power are always taken from the general supply and then placed on a bird; they are never moved from another bird.
20200323@Brown-Headed Cowbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190921@Brown-Headed Cowbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200323@Yellow-Billed Cuckoo.text: Eggs laid by any power are always taken from the general supply and then placed on a bird; they are never moved from another bird.

20200109b@Yellow-Billed Cuckoo.text: You may not use \textbf{Yellow-Billed Cuckoo}'s power to lay an [egg] on another player's bird.

20190921@Yellow-Billed Cuckoo.text: A bird with a [star] nest counts as any and all nest types at all times, including for egg-laying powers, bonus cards, and end-of-round goals, so \textbf{Yellow-Billed Cuckoo} may lay its [egg] on a [star] nest bird.
20190921@Yellow-Billed Cuckoo.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250524@Coal Tit.text: Food cached on \textbf{Coal Tit} counts as being in your supply only for the purpose of spending it; it does not satisfy powers that check what food is in your supply, and does not count toward the \textbf{Winter Feeder} bonus card.
20250524@Coal Tit.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210199b@Coal Tit.text: When a bird with a ``copy'' power (e.g., the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}) copies this bird's power, that bird retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on it until the end of the turn but no longer.

20200203@Coal Tit.text: Food cached on this bird is ``used'' (for points) and hence does not count as unused food when breaking point ties while scoring.

20200116@Coal Tit.text: You may spend a [seed] cached on this bird anytime you can spend a [seed] from your supply.

20250524@Eurasian Nuthatch.text: [seed] cached on \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch} is not in your supply, so it does not count toward the \textbf{Winter Feeder} bonus card even though you may spend it at any time.
20250524@Eurasian Nuthatch.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210199b@Eurasian Nuthatch.text: When a bird with a ``copy'' power (e.g., the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}) copies this bird's power, that bird retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on it until the end of the turn but no longer.

20200812@Eurasian Nuthatch.text: [seed] cached on \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch} by another bird's power (e.g., \textbf{European Magpie}) can later be spent using this bird's power, which applies to any [seed] cached on this card, not only [seed] it cached itself.
20200812@Eurasian Nuthatch.author: Joe Aubrey

20200203@Eurasian Nuthatch.text: Food cached on this bird is ``used'' (for points) and hence does not count as unused food when breaking point ties while scoring.

20200116@Eurasian Nuthatch.text: You may spend a [seed] cached on this bird anytime you can spend a [seed] from your supply.

20200127@Eleonora's Falcon.text: This bird's power is a [predator] power; the [predator] icon did not appear on the card in early printings, but the omission was corrected by April 2019.

20220322@Mute Swan.text: For the \textbf{birds with tucked [card]} end-of-round goal, count each of your birds with at least 1 card tucked beneath it. The [flocking] icon on the goal tile is synonymous with tucked cards; the powers of the birds involved are irrelevant, so it does not matter whether the bird has a [flocking] power or how the card came to be tucked there.
20220322@Mute Swan.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200127@Mute Swan.text: This bird's power is a [flocking] power; the [flocking] icon did not appear on the card in early printings, but the omission was corrected by April 2019.

20200208@Once between turns.text: You may not use a pink power during your turn (when an opponent performs an action that would otherwise enable using such a power).

20260107@Cetti's Warbler.text: \textbf{Cetti's Warbler} does not help toward the \textbf{different point values on birds} end-of-round goal: counting the same bird twice still accounts for only one point value, and the goal looks for birds with different point values.
20260107@Cetti's Warbler.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230709@Cetti's Warbler.text: \textbf{Cetti's Warbler}'s power applies only to the bird card itself, not to its duet token. Place a single duet token when you play \textbf{Cetti's Warbler}, just as with any other bird.
20230709@Cetti's Warbler.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200210@Cetti's Warbler.text: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities. When in your hand this card does not count toward end-of-round bonuses.

20200512@Eurasian Green Woodpecker.text: A round end (teal) power activates at the end of every round after the bird is played, not only the round in which it was played; a bird played in round 1 can activate its round end power in all four rounds. A ``this bird counts double toward the end-of-round goal'' power can give you a virtual 6th bird in a habitat when counting birds for the goal.
20200512@Eurasian Green Woodpecker.author: Joe Aubrey

20200210@Eurasian Green Woodpecker.text: This bird counts double toward precisely the end-of-round bonuses that count birds, not those that count other quantities. When in your hand this card does not count toward end-of-round bonuses.

20231122@Greylag Goose.text: When counting birds in a habitat for an end-of-round goal, \textbf{Greylag Goose} can push the total above 5: a bird that counts double may give you 6.
20231122@Greylag Goose.author: Joe Aubrey

20200210@Greylag Goose.text: \textbf{Greylag Goose} counts double toward precisely the end-of-round goals that count birds, not those that count other quantities. While in your hand this card does not count toward end-of-round goals.

20200222a@Citizen Scientist.text: In games where the Automa has drawn this bonus card, the Automa selects birds that have tucking powers; these powers are precisely those which contain the word ``tuck'' or ``tucked''.

2020022b@It becomes a tucked card.text: Cards whose powers include the phrase ``it becomes a tucked card'' (e.g., \textbf{Common Buzzard}) qualify for the \textbf{Citizen Scientist} bonus card when the Automa has drawn it.

20200330@Once between turns.text: If a pink power is triggered by a player using the ``gain food'', ``lay eggs'', or ``draw bird cards'' action, the pink power is resolved after the player collects the resources indicated on the player mat but before any brown powers in the corresponding row are activated. If a pink power is triggered by another bird's power, the pink power is resolved after the other bird's power has been resolved.

20200404@Resources.text: Whenever you are entitled to gain resources, you may choose to take some but not all of the quantity specified.
20200404@Resources.author: Joe Aubrey

20200405@Bird Counter.text: A bird with a [flocking] power qualifies for this bonus card regardless of the color of that power despite the specification of brown powers in this bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

20210321@Falconer.text: \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie} is not a predator bird and does not count for the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card; a bird is a predator only if it has the [predator] icon before its power text.
20210321@Falconer.author: Joe Aubrey

20200405@Falconer.text: A bird with a [predator] power qualifies for \textbf{Falconer} regardless of the color of that power, despite the specification of brown powers in this bonus card's Appendix entry.

20260124@Bonelli's Eagle.text: A bird played for free with \textbf{Yellow-Eyed Penguin}'s power still triggers its ``when played'' power, but powers that refer to a paid cost have no effect: \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} tucks no [card] when it is played for free.
20260124@Bonelli's Eagle.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250514@Bonelli's Eagle.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} copies only the ``When Played'' power itself, not the copied bird's food cost, so copying \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} does nothing because \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} has no [rodent] in its own cost. The copied power is also gone by the end of the turn, so it does not make \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} count toward the \textbf{Endangered Species} bonus card at game end.
20250514@Bonelli's Eagle.author: Joe Aubrey

20200405@Bonelli's Eagle.text: \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} counts toward the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's Appendix entry.

20210108b@Common Starling.text: You can spend the unused nectar from your personal supply as blue powers are activated before nectar is discarded.

20210301@Common Starling.text: The [wild] discarded for \textbf{Common Starling} may be a mix of any food types. Discarding food is a way of spending it, so [nectar] discarded for this power is placed on the appropriate spent nectar space of your player mat.
20210301@Common Starling.author: Joe Aubrey

20200405@Common Starling.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Bird Counter} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

20220523@Common Swift.text: The 2-for-1 food conversion may only be used when paying the food cost to play a bird card. It cannot be used to supply the [invertebrate] discarded for this bird's power; you must discard actual [invertebrate].

20240801@Common Swift.text: [nectar] cannot be used to pay the [invertebrate] discard for this bird's power. When a bird power refers to a specific food type, [nectar] is not a wild food.
20240801@Common Swift.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200111@Common Swift.text: The food types in these birds' powers are correct as printed; the specific food shown ([invertebrate] for \textbf{Common Swift}, [seed] for \textbf{House Sparrow}) applies, not ``any food''. 20200111@Common Swift.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210108b@Common Swift.text: You can spend the unused nectar from your personal supply as blue powers are activated before nectar is discarded.

20200405@Common Swift.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Bird Counter} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

20230516@Eastern Imperial Eagle.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} copies the power exactly as worded on the neighbor's bird onto itself for the duration of that turn only; at the end of the turn it no longer has that power. 20250514@Eastern Imperial Eagle.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} copies only the ``When Played'' power itself, not the copied bird's food cost. Treat the power as if it were printed on \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}: copying \textbf{Eastern Imperial Eagle} or \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} therefore does nothing, because \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} has no [rodent] in its own food cost.
20250514@Eastern Imperial Eagle.author: Joe Aubrey

20231208@Eastern Imperial Eagle.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230901@Eurasian Collared-Dove.text: [nectar] discarded to \textbf{Eurasian Collared-Dove}'s power goes to the ``spent nectar'' space for that habitat on the left side of your player mat (kept until the end of the game), not back to the supply.
20230901@Eurasian Collared-Dove.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200531@European Goldfinch.author: Joe Aubrey

20200405@European Goldfinch.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Bird Counter} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

20200405@Hooded Crow.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Bird Counter} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

20200204a@Horned Lark.text: A pink power activates directly after the action that triggered it, once the triggering player has finished all the actions on the card that caused it. 20200405@Ruff.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Bird Counter} bonus card despite the specification of brown powers in that bonus card's entry in the Appendix.

20200511@Alternative cost.text: If you use a bird's power to play in the same habitat a bird an alternative food cost specified via an asterisk next to its food cost, you may pay the alternative cost (which thus counts as paying the bird's ``normal food cost'') instead of paying its food cost.

20200712@Trade.text: ``Trading'' (e.g., when using the \textbf{Green Heron}'s power) counts as ``spending''.

20230621@Green Heron.text: [nectar] is an eligible food type for \textbf{Green Heron}'s power, so you may trade 1 [wild] for [nectar] from the supply. (An earlier official answer saying nectar was ineligible was retracted.)
20230621@Green Heron.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220509@Green Heron.text: When another player uses \textbf{Green Heron}'s power to trade a food token for [nectar], that counts as gaining [nectar], so \textbf{Spangled Drongo}'s power triggers. 20220509@Green Heron.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230101@Green Heron.text: Food traded away with \textbf{Green Heron} goes back to the supply, not to the birdfeeder; [nectar] traded away is spent instead, so place it in the spent-nectar space of your player mat.
20230101@Green Heron.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200719@Green Heron.text: You may not use this bird's power to trade a food token for a food token of the same type.

20200716a@Appendix.text: If information printed on a card conflicts with the card's appendix entry, the information on the card takes precedence. (See \textbf{American Oystercatcher}, \textbf{Belted Kingfisher}, and \textbf{Eastern Kingbird}.)

20200716a@Belted Kingfisher.text: This bird's power is triggered by another player playing a bird in their [wetland] during their turn, even when not using the ``play a bird'' card action to do so (instead using, e.g., the \textbf{Common Moorhen}'s power), despite this bird's entry in the Appendix.

20200716a@Common Moorhen.text: Using this bird's power to play a bird in your [wetland] triggers the power of the \textbf{Belted Kingfisher} on another player's player mat, despite the \textbf{Belted Kingfisher}'s entry in the Appendix.

20200716a@Eastern Kingbird.text: \textbf{Eastern Kingbird}'s power triggers whenever another player plays a bird in their [forest] on their turn, even without using the ``play a bird'' action (e.g. via \textbf{Goldcrest}'s power), despite this bird's Appendix entry.

20200710@Eastern Kingbird.text: Playing a bird is not the same as activating a bird. This bird's power is not triggered when another player moves an existing bird into their [forest]; only when a new bird is played there.
20200710@Eastern Kingbird.author: Joe Aubrey

20200716a@Goldcrest.text: Using this bird's power to play a bird in your [forest] triggers the power of the \textbf{Eastern Kingbird} on another player's player mat, despite the \textbf{Eastern Kingbird}'s entry in the Appendix.

20200716a@Short-Toed Treecreeper.text: Using this bird's power to play a bird in your [forest] triggers the power of the \textbf{Eastern Kingbird} on another player's player mat, despite the \textbf{Eastern Kingbird}'s entry in the Appendix.

20200716b@[wild] [wild] $\\Rightarrow$ [.text: You may substitute 2 [wild] for any 1 food in a bird's food cost whenever you play a bird, including outside the scope of the ``play a bird'' action.

20201003@Discard pile.text: Cards discarded to the discard pile are placed face up.

20201003@Discard pile#2.text: Players may look through the discard pile at any time.

20201009@Honey.text: As of the release of the Oceania Expansion, \textit{honey} is no longer a keyword for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.

20240225@European Honey Buzzard.text: When a power resets the birdfeeder, such as \textbf{European Honey Buzzard}, all 5 dice are rerolled, including dice that players had already removed from the birdfeeder. This matches resetting the birdfeeder when all dice in it show the same face.
20240225@European Honey Buzzard.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250410@European Honey Buzzard.text: Dice showing the [invertebrate]/[seed] face count: \textbf{European Honey Buzzard} gains the [invertebrate] from such a die along with all other [invertebrate] showing (and \textbf{Hawfinch} may take the [seed] from such a die).
20250410@European Honey Buzzard.author: Joe Aubrey

20201009@European Honey Buzzard.text: As of the release of the Oceania Expansion, \textit{honey} is no longer a keyword for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card, and hence this bird no longer qualifies for it.

20201009@Lewin's Honeyeater.text: As of the release of the Oceania Expansion, \textit{honey} is no longer a keyword for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card, and hence this bird do not qualify for it.

20201009@New Holland Honeyeater.text: As of the release of the Oceania Expansion, \textit{honey} is no longer a keyword for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card, and hence this bird do not qualify for it.

20201009@Rufous-Banded Honeyeater.text: As of the release of the Oceania Expansion, \textit{honey} is no longer a keyword for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card, but \textit{rufous} is a keyword, and hence this bird qualifies for that bonus card.

20220605@Eastern Rosella.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo} only triggers between your turns, never on your own turn. If you activate \textbf{Eastern Rosella} on your turn, causing all players to gain 1 [nectar], \textbf{Spangled Drongo} does not activate.
20220605@Eastern Rosella.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201010@Eastern Rosella.text: \textbf{Eastern Rosella} counts toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card.

20201010@Emu.text: When using this bird's power, you must gain all [seed] available in the birdfeeder, since some of it may be allocated to other players.

20201010@Southern Cassowary.text: When using this bird's power to discard another bird from your mat, all food cached on that bird, [egg] laid on that bird, and [card] tucked under that bird are discarded.

20201011@Site Selection Expert.text: When scoring this bonus card, birds played sideways can count toward a nest type in both of the columns in which they were played. A [star] nest on a sideways bird can count as different nest types in the two columns in which it was played.

20210107@Site Selection Expert.text: \textbf{Brown-Headed Cowbird} has no nest type, so it does not count toward the \textbf{Site Selection Expert} bonus card; it is not treated as a [star] nest.
20210107@Site Selection Expert.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201116a@End of Round Reference.text: When playing with the Oceania Expansion, follow the order of steps on the (Oceania Expansion) End of Round Reference, not the order given in the Oceania Expansion rulebook.

20201116a@Game end.text: When playing with the Oceania Expansion, follow the order of steps on the (Oceania Expansion) End of Round Reference, not the order given in the Oceania Expansion rulebook.

20240110@Superb Lyrebird.text: Copy powers act as if the copied text were printed on the copying bird. So if \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} copies the \textbf{Northern Mockingbird}'s power, you then repeat a brown power on another bird in \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}'s own habitat ([forest]).
20240110@Superb Lyrebird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201116b@Superb Lyrebird.text: If you copy the power of a bird that lets it move to another habitat---and \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} satisfies applicable conditions (e.g., being the rightmost bird in its habitat)---it may move to that habitat, even one in which it cannot be played.

20210119a@Superb Lyrebird.text: When a bird (e.g., the \textbf{Gray Catbird}) repeats this bird's power, it repeats the copying power printed on this bird and not any powers this bird repeated earlier in the turn. Since being a predator power is a property of a power, this bird copying a predator power and the power succeeding counts as success of a predator power (e.g., for purposes of enabling the activation of a pink power on another player's mat, like that of the \textbf{Black Vulture}).

20210199b@Superb Lyrebird.text: When this bird copies another bird's power, it retains any effects specified in the copied bird's power text as long as those effects may occur but not beyond the end of the turn. (So, e.g., if it copies the \textbf{Coal Tit}'s power, it retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on this bird until the end of the turn but no longer, and if copies the \textbf{Wood Duck}'s power, the copied power still obligates you to discard a card at the end of your turn.)

20210108a@Superb Lyrebird.text: \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} counts towards the \textbf{Forester} bonus card even though it can potentially fly elsewhere.

20201116b@Tūī.text: If \textbf{Tūī} copies a power that lets a bird move to another habitat---and it satisfies applicable conditions (e.g., being the rightmost bird in its habitat)---it may move to that habitat, even one in which it cannot be played.

20210199b@Tūī.text: When \textbf{Tūī} copies another bird's power, it retains any effects specified in the copied bird's power text as long as those effects may occur but not beyond the end of the turn. (So, e.g., if it copies the \textbf{Coal Tit}'s power, it retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on this bird until the end of the turn but no longer, and if copies the \textbf{Wood Duck}'s power, the copied power still obligates you to discard a card at the end of your turn.)

20210199a@Tūī.text: When a bird (e.g., the \textbf{Gray Catbird}) repeats \textbf{Tūī}'s power, it repeats the copying power printed here and not any powers this bird repeated earlier in the turn. Since being a predator power is a property of a power, copying a predator power and succeeding counts as a predator success (e.g., enabling a pink power like \textbf{Black Vulture}'s).

20210108a@Tūī.text: This bird counts towards \textbf{Forester} bonus card even though it can potentially fly elsewhere.

20201117@Discard.text: ``Discarding'' food while resolving a bird power counts as ``spending''.

20201204@Forest Data Analyst.text: This bonus card only awards points for a single sequence of bird cards of increasing or decreasing wingspan.

20201204@Grassland Data Analyst.text: This bonus card only awards points for a single sequence of bird cards of increasing or decreasing wingspan.

20201229@Wetland Data Analyst.text: Adjacent birds with the exact same wingspan count as part of an ascending or descending sequence for this bonus card.
20201229@Wetland Data Analyst.author: Joe Aubrey

20201204@Wetland Data Analyst.text: This bonus card only awards points for a single sequence of bird cards of increasing or decreasing wingspan.

20210101@Giving.text: ``Giving'' a resource to another player does not count as ``spending''.

20210101@Red-Winged Parrot.text: Giving [nectar] to another player with this power does not count as ``spending'', so do not add that nectar to the ``spent nectar'' space for its habitat.

20201206@Red-Winged Parrot.text: Being given [nectar] by \textbf{Red-Winged Parrot} counts as gaining [nectar] for the receiving player, so it may activate another player's \textbf{Spangled Drongo}, which triggers on a [nectar] gain by any means and not only on the ``gain food'' action.
20201206@Red-Winged Parrot.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210199a@Copy.text: When a bird (e.g., the \textbf{Gray Catbird}) repeats the power of a bird with a ``copy'' power (e.g., the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}), it repeats the copying power printed on that bird and not any powers that bird repeated earlier in the turn.

20210199a@Copy#2.text: Since being a predator power is a property of a power, a bird with a ``copy'' power copying a predator power and the power succeedings counts as success of a predator power (e.g., for purposes of enabling the activation of a pink power on another player's mat, like that of the \textbf{Black Vulture}. In particular, even if the copying bird is in the same habitat as the \textbf{Hooded Merganser}, that latter bird cannot repeat this bird's power, since the power printed on this card is not a predator power.

20210199a@Repeat.text: When a bird with a ``repeat'' power (e.g., the \textbf{Gray Catbird}) repeats the power of a bird with a ``copy'' power (e.g., the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird}), it repeats the power printed on the bird with the ``copy'' power and not any powers that bird copied earlier in the turn.

20210199b@Copy.text: When a bird with a ``copy'' power copies another bird's power, it retains any effects specified in the copied bird's power text as long as those effects may occur but not beyond the end of the turn. (So, e.g., if the \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} copies the \textbf{Coal Tit}'s power, the former bird retains the ability to spend [seed] cached on it until the end of the turn but no longer, and if it instead copies the \textbf{Wood Duck}'s power, the copied power still obligates you to discard a card at the end of your turn.)

20210206@Beak pointing left/right.text: A bird played horizontally qualifies for one of \textbf{Beak pointing left/right} end-of-round goals if and only if it would count were the card played in its vertical orientation.

20210318@Beak pointing left/right.text: This bird counts double for \textbf{Beak pointing left/right} if it qualifies for the goal.

20190405@Loggerhead Shrike.text: Activating a bird's power is not the same as taking the corresponding action. A bird activated by another power that gains [rodent] does not trigger \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike}, because the ``gain food'' action was not taken; likewise, a bird moved to another habitat by a bird power is not being played, so no [egg] cost is paid for the column it moves into.
20190405@Loggerhead Shrike.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191218@Loggerhead Shrike.text: \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike} is not triggered by [rodent] gained from a ``when activated'' bird power, such as \textbf{Eastern Screech-Owl}'s, even when that power fires during another player's ``gain food'' action.
20191218@Loggerhead Shrike.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260708@Loggerhead Shrike.text: \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike} triggers only when another player gains [rodent] as part of the ``gain food'' core action of the [forest] habitat, not from [rodent] gained or cached by bird powers.
20260708@Loggerhead Shrike.author: Joe Aubrey

20190416@Osprey.text: Powers are optional: the owner of \textbf{Osprey} may choose not to activate its power at all, in which case no player gains a [fish].
20190416@Osprey.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20211129@Fishery Manager.text: Only birds printed with the [fish] icon count for \textbf{Fishery Manager}; a bird whose food cost shows only a [wild] (any food type) symbol does not count.
20211129@Fishery Manager.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200125@Nest Box Builder.text: A [star] nest counts toward end-of-round goals in every round of the game: a bird whose [star] counted toward a nest goal in one round still counts toward a nest goal in a later round.
20200125@Nest Box Builder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190629@Nest Box Builder.text: A bird with a [star] nest counts as any nest type, so it counts toward every bonus card whose nest requirement it can satisfy, and toward more than one of them at the same time.
20190629@Nest Box Builder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200125@Platform Builder.text: A [star] nest counts toward end-of-round goals in every round of the game: a bird whose [star] counted toward a nest goal in one round still counts toward a nest goal in a later round.
20200125@Platform Builder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190629@Platform Builder.text: A bird with a [star] nest counts as any nest type, so it counts toward every bonus card whose nest requirement it can satisfy, and toward more than one of them at the same time.
20190629@Platform Builder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200423@Blue Jay.text: The choice to cache cannot be changed later. Contrast \textbf{Sandhill Crane}, where discarding 1 [seed] is a cost you may not substitute or skip.
20200423@Blue Jay.author: Joe Aubrey

20200423@Acorn Woodpecker.text: Once you have chosen whether to cache the [seed] gained with this power or keep it in your personal supply, the choice cannot be changed later.
20200423@Acorn Woodpecker.author: Joe Aubrey

20200423@Steller's Jay.text: Once you have chosen whether to cache the [seed] gained with this power or keep it in your personal supply, the choice cannot be changed later.
20200423@Steller's Jay.author: Joe Aubrey

20231126@Blue Jay.text: ``May'' is a binary option: do exactly as instructed or not at all, never a substitution. On \textbf{Blue Jay} you may cache the gained [seed] on this bird or keep it in your personal supply, since you have already gained it.
20231126@Blue Jay.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190901@Blue Jay.text: Caching the [seed] is optional; you may instead keep it as a food token to spend.
20190901@Blue Jay.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191007@Fish Crow.text: For the \textbf{food cost of played birds} end-of-round goal, the clarification to count only 1 food for birds with a choice in their food cost refers to the ``/'' in food costs. \textbf{Song Sparrow} ([invertebrate]/[seed]/[fruit]) counts as 1, while \textbf{Fish Crow} ([fish]+[wild]) counts as 2.
20191007@Fish Crow.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230610@Viticulturalist.text: \textbf{Viticulturalist} counts only birds showing the [fruit] icon; [wild] and [nectar] icons do not count for it.
20230610@Viticulturalist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200327@Viticulturalist.text: Birds that eat [wild] do not count toward \textbf{Viticulturalist}; only birds showing the [fruit] icon qualify. This applies to every food-based bonus card.
20200327@Viticulturalist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191218@Eastern Screech-Owl.text: Food gained from a ``when activated'' power such as \textbf{Eastern Screech-Owl}'s does not trigger \textbf{Loggerhead Shrike}, which refers only to the core benefit of the ``gain food'' action.
20191218@Eastern Screech-Owl.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210327@Eastern Screech-Owl.text: \textbf{Eastern Screech-Owl}'s beak does not point in either direction, so it counts for neither the \textbf{beaks pointing left} nor the \textbf{beaks pointing right} end-of-round goal. (This is listed on page 11 of the Oceania rules.)
20210327@Eastern Screech-Owl.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240207@Ecologist.text: Score only one habitat for the \textbf{Ecologist} bonus card, even if two or three habitats are tied for the fewest birds; the maximum score is therefore 10 points.
20240207@Ecologist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20241129@Ecologist.text: A habitat with no birds counts as your habitat with the fewest birds (0 birds), so an empty habitat scores 0 points.
20241129@Ecologist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260116@Ecologist.text: Hummingbird cards are birds and count toward bonus cards in the ordinary way, including \textbf{Bird Bander}, \textbf{Ecologist}, \textbf{Ethologist}, \textbf{Passerine Specialist}, \textbf{Small Clutch Specialist}, and the Data Analyst and Ranger bonus cards.
20260116@Ecologist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200110@Eurasian Nutcracker.text: The [seed] cached by \textbf{Eurasian Nutcracker} comes from your personal supply of food you have gathered, not from the general supply.
20200110@Eurasian Nutcracker.author: Joe Aubrey

20211023@Turkey Vulture.text: \textbf{Turkey Vulture} is not a [predator] bird; its [predator] symbol appears within the power text rather than before it. A predator ``succeeds'' when another player's [predator] power results in that player gaining a benefit - for example, revealing a card whose wingspan is less than the stated value and tucking it.
20211023@Turkey Vulture.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200522@Turkey Vulture.text: A [predator] ``succeeds'' when its action is successful, not when the bird is played - usually meaning it caches a food or tucks a card. If a bird such as \textbf{Northern Goshawk} uses its power to tuck cards instead of paying some or all of its food cost, that counts as both tucking a card and a [predator] succeeding, and triggers pink powers accordingly.
20200522@Turkey Vulture.author: Joe Aubrey

20210104@Turkey Vulture.text: Gaining food from the birdfeeder with the \textbf{Sacred Kingfisher}'s power counts as a successful [predator] action, so it can trigger \textbf{Turkey Vulture}. It cannot trigger the pink power of the player whose turn it is, because the \textbf{Sacred Kingfisher}'s power resolves as the final step of that player's turn, not between turns.
20210104@Turkey Vulture.author: Joe Aubrey

20200204a@Turkey Vulture.text: A pink power activates directly after the action that triggered it, once the triggering player has finished all the actions on the card that caused it. The player with the pink power completes it before the original player continues activating any further birds in their row.
20200204a@Turkey Vulture.author: Joe Aubrey

20200331@Turkey Vulture.text: ``Turkey'' does not count as a geography term for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, and neither does ``turkey vulture'' (turkey vultures are named after the bird, not the country).
20200331@Turkey Vulture.author: Joe Aubrey

20201010a@Hooded Warbler.text: [nectar] may be substituted for any of the 5 other food types when paying the food cost to play a bird. For example, \textbf{Hooded Warbler} costs [invertebrate][invertebrate], so it can be played by paying [invertebrate][invertebrate], [invertebrate][nectar], or [nectar][nectar].
20201010a@Hooded Warbler.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200301@Hooded Warbler.text: \textbf{Hooded Warbler} has no power, so nothing happens when an action cube passes over it while activating birds.
20200301@Hooded Warbler.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250704@Bird Feeder.text: Birds that eat [wild] do not count toward \textbf{Bird Feeder}; bonus cards that name a specific food icon only count birds showing that icon.
20250704@Bird Feeder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221106@Bird Feeder.text: The food [die] symbol always means, ``Remove a die from the birdfeeder and gain the food noted on it from the supply.''
20221106@Bird Feeder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200322@American Bittern.text: \textbf{American Bittern}'s power is optional: if activating it would not benefit the player who activated it (for example, if that player does not have the fewest birds in their [wetland]), they may choose not to activate it at all.
20200322@American Bittern.author: Joe Aubrey

20200331@Wild Turkey.text: ``Turkey'' does not count as a geography term for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, and neither does ``turkey vulture'' (turkey vultures are named after the bird, not the country).
20200331@Wild Turkey.author: Joe Aubrey

20201104@Wild Turkey.text: The \textbf{white \& no powers} end-of-round goal counts both birds with ``when played'' powers (white cards, e.g. \textbf{Common Blackbird}) and birds with no powers at all (e.g. \textbf{American Woodcock}, \textbf{Wild Turkey}).
20201104@Wild Turkey.author: Joe Aubrey

20200420@Anna's Hummingbird.text: Any player may decline to take food from the birdfeeder when this bird's power is activated, and they do not get a second chance during that activation.
20200420@Anna's Hummingbird.author: Joe Aubrey

20200405a@Anna's Hummingbird.text: You may choose yourself as the player who gains food first.
20200405a@Anna's Hummingbird.author: Joe Aubrey

20200411@Eurasian Tree Sparrow.text: ``Gain food'' here means only the basic action, not gaining food (or laying eggs) from a card power.
20200411@Eurasian Tree Sparrow.author: Joe Aubrey

20200725@Eurasian Tree Sparrow.text: If the birdfeeder contains no [seed] you gain nothing, but the power still counts as used and cannot be activated again until after your next turn. Whether the birdfeeder was reset first is irrelevant.
20200725@Eurasian Tree Sparrow.author: Joe Aubrey

20230309@Ethologist.text: At the end of the game, choose one habitat (row), ignore the other two, and score 2 points for each \textit{distinct} power color present in that row (including white/no power), not 2 points per bird. Multiple birds of the same color score that color only once, so 4 brown and 1 white bird score 4 points; the maximum is 8 points, from at least 4 birds of 4 different colors in one row.
20230309@Ethologist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260116@Ethologist.text: Hummingbird cards are birds and count toward bonus cards in the ordinary way, including \textbf{Ethologist}.
20260116@Ethologist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201002@Ruby-Throated Hummingbird.text: [nectar] is wild for playing birds and may be spent for any food in a bird's cost, including a single [nectar] to pay a cost of 1 [seed], but cannot be substituted when a bird's power refers to a specific food type.
20201002@Ruby-Throated Hummingbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200420@Ruby-Throated Hummingbird.text: Any player may decline to take food from the birdfeeder when this power is activated, and they do not get a second chance during that activation.
20200420@Ruby-Throated Hummingbird.author: Joe Aubrey

20230909@Ruby-Throated Hummingbird.text: ``The player of your choice'' includes yourself, so you may take the first [die] from the birdfeeder.
20230909@Ruby-Throated Hummingbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200422@European Robin.text: \textbf{European Robin}'s power only applies at the moment it is activated: gain 1 food of a type you have already gained earlier in that same turn (for example, food gained by placing the action cube in the [forest] before moving the cube left onto this bird). It does not grant extra food at any other time.
20200422@European Robin.author: Joe Aubrey

20211123@Sandhill Crane.text: [nectar] cannot be substituted for a specific food type demanded by a bird power; \textbf{Sandhill Crane}'s ``Discard 1 [seed]'' must be paid with [seed].
20211123@Sandhill Crane.author: Joe Aubrey

20200430@Red-Legged Partridge.text: You may activate this bird's power even if one or more birds in the column already have the maximum number of [egg] they can hold; lay [egg] on the birds that can receive them.
20200430@Red-Legged Partridge.author: Joe Aubrey

20200508@Clark's Grebe.text: You do not need to reserve a [card] in hand to satisfy \textbf{Clark's Grebe}'s power; if you end your turn with no [card] in hand, there is nothing to discard and that is fine.
20200508@Clark's Grebe.author: Joe Aubrey

20220826@Common Raven.text: The [wild] symbol always includes [nectar], so \textbf{Common Raven} may take [nectar] from the supply; you are never obligated to choose it. The Oceania rulebook suggests removing \textbf{Common Raven} and \textbf{Chihuahuan Raven} from the deck if players find this too powerful.
20220826@Common Raven.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200623@Common Raven.text: The 2 [wild] may be two food tokens of the same type or of two different types.
20200623@Common Raven.author: Joe Aubrey

20200703@American Crow.text: \textbf{Rodentologist} counts only birds with the [rodent] symbol specifically; a [wild] food symbol (e.g., \textbf{American Crow}) does not count.
20200703@American Crow.author: Joe Aubrey

20201002@Mourning Dove.text: [nectar] is wild for playing birds and may be spent for any food in a bird's cost, including a single [nectar] to pay a cost of 1 [seed]. [nectar] cannot be substituted when a bird's power refers to a specific food type.
20201002@Mourning Dove.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250912@Kākāpō.text: When the order of Game End powers matters, activate them in clockwise order starting with the player who has the first-player token.
20250912@Kākāpō.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201005@Kākāpō.text: Using a yellow (game end) power is optional; you may choose not to activate it.
20201005@Kākāpō.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201006@Great Horned Owl.text: \textbf{Great Horned Owl}'s beak points straight forward, neither left nor right; the rulebook's list of such birds includes it.
20201006@Great Horned Owl.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220804@Wrybill.text: A bonus card discarded to score \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane} goes to the discarded bonus card pile and may be retrieved later with \textbf{Wrybill}, allowing the same bonus card to be scored twice.
20220804@Wrybill.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220903@Wrybill.text: \textbf{Wrybill} counts as pointing left for goals and bonus cards that care about bill direction: although the bird faces straight ahead, its bill points toward the left side of the card. What matters is the bill, not the bird's face. The rulebook lists the birds that face forward but whose beaks point left or right.
20220903@Wrybill.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201008@Pūkeko.text: Adjacent birds are those immediately to the left, right, above, or below the bird in question.
20201008@Pūkeko.author: Joe Aubrey

20201020@Common Cuckoo.text: \textbf{Common Cuckoo} correctly has no nest type and no egg limit; as a brood parasite it lays its eggs in other birds' nests, matching its power.
20201020@Common Cuckoo.author: Joe Aubrey

20241223@Sacred Kingfisher.text: Gaining food from the birdfeeder with \textbf{Sacred Kingfisher}'s power counts as a successful [predator] action, so it can trigger another player's power that responds to a successful predator (e.g. \textbf{Turkey Vulture}). It cannot trigger the pink power of the player whose turn it is, because \textbf{Sacred Kingfisher}'s power resolves as the final step of that player's turn, not between turns.
20241223@Sacred Kingfisher.author: Joe Aubrey

20201104@American Woodcock.text: The \textbf{white \& no powers} end-of-round goal counts both birds with ``when played'' powers (white cards, e.g. \textbf{Common Blackbird}) and birds with no powers at all (e.g. \textbf{American Woodcock}, \textbf{Wild Turkey}).
20201104@American Woodcock.author: Joe Aubrey

20210330@Breeding Manager.text: Count only [egg] tokens sitting on a bird card at game end; eggs printed on the card art do not count.
20210330@Breeding Manager.author: Joe Aubrey

20201104a@Breeding Manager.text: Any bird with 4 or more [egg] on it at game end counts; the number does not have to be exactly 4.
20201104a@Breeding Manager.author: Joe Aubrey

20201116@Canvasback.text: \textit{Back} is a body part for this bonus card, as listed in the \textit{European Expansion} rulebook (``Anatomist (birds with body parts in their names): back, leg, toe''), so \textbf{Canvasback} counts toward it.
20201116@Canvasback.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240115@Galah.text: The two clauses of \textbf{Galah}'s power are independent; the order is simply order of operations. Even if the chosen player does not find a [seed] in the birdfeeder, you still tuck 2 [card] from the deck behind this bird.
20240115@Galah.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201203a@Black-Billed Magpie.text: If another player activates \textbf{Laughing Kookaburra}'s [predator] power and it succeeds (they gain a food), \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie}'s power triggers and you gain 1 [die] from the birdfeeder.
20201203a@Black-Billed Magpie.author: Joe Aubrey

20210321@Black-Billed Magpie.text: \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie} is not a predator bird and does not count for the \textbf{Falconer} bonus card; a bird is a predator only if it has the [predator] icon before its power text.
20210321@Black-Billed Magpie.author: Joe Aubrey

20201203a@Laughing Kookaburra.text: \textbf{Laughing Kookaburra} has a [predator] power. If another player activates it and it succeeds (they gain a food), \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie}'s power triggers and you gain 1 [die] from the birdfeeder.
20201203a@Laughing Kookaburra.author: Joe Aubrey

20220826@Chihuahuan Raven.text: The [wild] symbol always includes [nectar], so \textbf{Chihuahuan Raven} may take [nectar] from the supply with its power. The Oceania rulebook suggests that players who find this too powerful remove \textbf{Chihuahuan Raven} and \textbf{Common Raven} from the deck when playing with the Oceania Expansion.
20220826@Chihuahuan Raven.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201204a@Chihuahuan Raven.text: The [wild] (``any food'') symbol includes [nectar] among the foods you may choose, but you are never obligated to choose [nectar].
20201204a@Chihuahuan Raven.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201205@Grey Shrikethrush.text: [nectar] is wild for paying bird costs and may be spent in place of any specific food, but a [nectar] icon in a cost must be paid with [nectar]; only a [wild] icon accepts any food.
20201205@Grey Shrikethrush.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220605@Spangled Drongo.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo} only triggers between your turns, never on your own turn. If you activate \textbf{Eastern Rosella} on your turn, causing all players to gain 1 [nectar], \textbf{Spangled Drongo} does not activate.
20220605@Spangled Drongo.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220509@Spangled Drongo.text: When another player uses \textbf{Green Heron}'s power to trade a food token for [nectar], that counts as gaining [nectar], so \textbf{Spangled Drongo} triggers - it is not a net gain of food, but it is still a gain.
20220509@Spangled Drongo.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230722@Spangled Drongo.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo} triggers when another player gains [nectar] from the supply by discarding [fruit] with \textbf{Mistletoebird}'s power.
20230722@Spangled Drongo.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20241228@Spangled Drongo.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo} triggers whenever another player gains [nectar] by any means, not only with the ``gain food'' action - for example, if another player gains 1 [nectar] from the supply through a bird power. As a ``once between turns'' power, it can trigger only once between each of your turns.
20241228@Spangled Drongo.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220820@Kea.text: Deciding how many additional bonus cards to draw, and discarding the corresponding [wild], is a one-time decision, so you cannot discard food one at a time.
20220820@Kea.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230329@Kea.text: You look at the first bonus card drawn with \textbf{Kea}'s power before deciding how many additional bonus cards to draw.
20230329@Kea.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210403@Kea.text: You keep only 1 bonus card out of all those drawn with this power, including the first one drawn before discarding [wild].
20210403@Kea.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201230a@Mechanical Engineer.text: A bonus card with tiered scoring awards only the amount for the tier reached, not points per qualifying bird. On \textbf{Cartographer} you must have at least 2 qualifying birds to score 3 points and at least 4 to score 7 points.
20201230a@Mechanical Engineer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201227@Mechanical Engineer.text: Only one scoring category on a bonus card is scored: score either for 1 set of the 4 nest types or for 2 or more sets, not both.
20201227@Mechanical Engineer.author: Joe Aubrey

20210117@Korimako.text: The [rodent] discarded for \textbf{Korimako}'s power cannot be cached food; cached food may only be spent when a card specifically refers to it, and otherwise is only worth points.
20210117@Korimako.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230109@Korimako.text: The [rodent] come from your own personal supply, not from the birdfeeder; throughout the rulebook, ``discard'' refers to paying food from your supply.
20230109@Korimako.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210123@Australian Shelduck.text: This bird's power allows resetting or refilling the tray only once; you may not keep resetting until a [cavity] or [star] nest bird appears.
20210123@Australian Shelduck.author: Joe Aubrey

20240903@Forster's Tern.text: The card drawn with \textbf{Forster's Tern} goes into your hand; \textbf{Great Crested Grebe} and \textbf{Wilson's Storm Petrel} work differently, keeping their drawn cards separate from your hand until the end of your turn, when you keep 1 and discard the rest.
20240903@Forster's Tern.author: Joe Aubrey

20210124@Forster's Tern.text: \textbf{Forster's Tern} requires discarding from your hand, so if your hand is empty at the end of your turn (for instance because you tucked all your cards with \textbf{Common Chiffchaff}), you discard nothing.
20210124@Forster's Tern.author: Joe Aubrey

20231204@Common Chiffchaff.text: You do not need to keep a card in hand to satisfy \textbf{Wood Duck}'s power. If you draw 2 [card] with \textbf{Wood Duck} and then play or tuck all the cards in your hand (for example with \textbf{Common Chiffchaff}), having no card to discard at the end of your turn is legal.
20231204@Common Chiffchaff.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210124@Common Chiffchaff.text: Tucking all your cards with \textbf{Common Chiffchaff} can leave your hand empty, in which case \textbf{Forster's Tern}'s end-of-turn discard discards nothing.
20210124@Common Chiffchaff.author: Joe Aubrey

20210124@Common Chaffinch.text: Tucking all your cards with \textbf{Common Chaffinch} can leave your hand empty, in which case an end-of-turn discard such as \textbf{Forster's Tern}'s discards nothing.
20210124@Common Chaffinch.author: Joe Aubrey

20210127@Bluethroat.text: [nectar] counts as a food type for this bird's power, so you may choose [nectar] and all players gain 1 [nectar] from the supply.
20210127@Bluethroat.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20241229@Brown Falcon.text: A [wild] food cost symbol does not count as an [invertebrate] or a [rodent] for \textbf{Brown Falcon}: a card whose food cost includes only [wild] is discarded rather than tucked.
20241229@Brown Falcon.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210130@California Quail.text: For end-of-round goals that name two food types in the food cost of your birds, count every icon of either type printed in the food costs of your played birds; a single bird does not need to require both. For example, with 5 [fruit] icons and 8 [seed] icons among your played birds, your number for the goal is 13.
20210130@California Quail.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210130@Cassin's Finch.text: For end-of-round goals that name two food types in the food cost of your birds, count every icon of either type printed in the food costs of your played birds; a single bird does not need to require both. For example, with 5 [fruit] icons and 8 [seed] icons among your played birds, your number for the goal is 13.
20210130@Cassin's Finch.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231204@Wood Duck.text: You do not need to keep a card in hand to discard: if you draw 2 [card] with \textbf{Wood Duck} and then play or tuck your whole hand (for example with \textbf{Common Chiffchaff}), having nothing to discard at the end of your turn is legal.
20231204@Wood Duck.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210130@Wood Duck.text: For end-of-round goals that name two food types in the food cost of your birds, count every icon of either type printed in the food costs of your played birds; a single bird does not need to require both. For example, with 5 [fruit] icons and 8 [seed] icons among your played birds, your number for the goal is 13.
20210130@Wood Duck.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210306@Plains-Wanderer.text: When counting birds in your [grassland] for this bird's power, include \textbf{Plains-Wanderer} itself. If it were excluded, the power would say ``each other bird''.
20210306@Plains-Wanderer.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210321a@Gould's Finch.text: With no open space in the habitat for the bird, you cannot use \textbf{Gould's Finch}'s power at all: if you can't play the bird, you don't get to use its ``when played'' or ``game end'' power either.
20210321a@Gould's Finch.author: Joe Aubrey

20260728@Gould's Finch.text: When a bird is played using a ``game end'' (yellow) power such as \textbf{Dovekie} or \textbf{Yellow-Eyed Penguin}, you still gain the benefits of its ``when played'' (white) and ``game end'' (yellow) powers, even if the yellow power does not say so. \textbf{Gould's Finch} states this explicitly only for extra clarity.
20260728@Gould's Finch.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220605a@Grey-Headed Mannikin.text: Nectar in your personal supply is returned to the supply during step 2 of the end of round 6, before ``game end'' powers such as \textbf{Grey-Headed Mannikin}'s are activated, so that nectar is no longer available to help pay the food cost of the bird played with this power.
20220605a@Grey-Headed Mannikin.author: Jamey Stegmaier
