20210321a@Grey-Headed Mannikin.text: With no open space in the habitat for the bird, you cannot use \textbf{Grey-Headed Mannikin}'s power at all: if you can't play the bird, you don't get to use its ``when played'' or ``game end'' power either.
20210321a@Grey-Headed Mannikin.author: Joe Aubrey

20260728@Grey-Headed Mannikin.text: When a bird is played using a ``game end'' (yellow) power such as \textbf{Dovekie} or \textbf{Yellow-Eyed Penguin}, you still gain the benefits of its ``when played'' (white) and ``game end'' (yellow) powers, even if the yellow power does not say so. \textbf{Grey-Headed Mannikin} states this explicitly only for extra clarity.
20260728@Grey-Headed Mannikin.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210624@Black-Shouldered Kite.text: The player you give the [rodent] to must accept it; they cannot decline in order to prevent you from laying eggs.
20210624@Black-Shouldered Kite.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230321@Black-Shouldered Kite.text: All 3 [egg] are laid at once as part of resolving the power, essentially ``lay 3 [egg] on this bird if you can''; eggs already on the bird may limit its remaining egg capacity.
20230321@Black-Shouldered Kite.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210805@Wedge-Tailed Eagle.text: The condition ``If its wingspan is over 65cm'' is correct and not a misprint; unlike other predators, this bird tucks the drawn [card] when the wingspan is large.
20210805@Wedge-Tailed Eagle.author: Joe Aubrey

20210823@Australian Magpie.text: End-of-round goals are scored before end-of-game powers are activated (steps 4 and 6 of the ``End of Round Reference'' tile included with the \textit{Oceania Expansion}). Score the end-of-round goal first, then activate \textbf{Australian Magpie}, so discarding [egg] with its power cannot change your score for an egg-based goal.
20210823@Australian Magpie.author: Joe Aubrey

20210902@Clark's Nutcracker.text: The gained [seed] goes to your personal supply unless you choose to cache it on this bird; caching is optional.
20210902@Clark's Nutcracker.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20211213@Blyth's Hornbill.text: A bird with a [star] (wild) nest counts as having a [cavity] nest for \textbf{Blyth's Hornbill}, so you may discard all [egg] from a bird with a [star] nest.
20211213@Blyth's Hornbill.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220111@Budgerigar.text: \textbf{Budgerigar} is a brown ``when activated'' bird; the Oceania appendix listing it as ``when played'' is an error.
20220111@Budgerigar.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231010@Budgerigar.text: A [star] wingspan bird may be treated as any wingspan you choose at the moment it matters, so you may decide whether a [star] bird in the tray counts as the smallest bird.
20231010@Budgerigar.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220130@Spotless Crake.text: You are always limited by the [egg] limit of each bird, including when laying [egg] with an end-of-round or game-end power; if the birds in your [wetland] are already at their [egg] limit, no [egg] can be laid.
20220130@Spotless Crake.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231229@Black Vulture.text: A [predator] power ``succeeds'' when its element of chance produces the result it is looking for (for example, looking at the top card of the deck and finding a bird with a small enough wingspan to tuck). \textbf{Black Vulture}'s power triggers whenever another player's [predator] finds what it is looking for.
20231229@Black Vulture.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220209@Black Vulture.text: Activate this power immediately when another player's [predator] succeeds, not at the end of that player's turn.
20220209@Black Vulture.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220213a@American White Pelican.text: You must discard an actual [fish] to activate \textbf{American White Pelican}; food substitutions only apply when playing a bird, not when paying a cost in a bird's power.
20220213a@American White Pelican.author: Joe Aubrey

20220305@Common Loon.text: Zero birds counts as the fewest birds, so a player with no birds in their [wetland] can be the player with the fewest birds and draw 1 [card].
20220305@Common Loon.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220411@Royal Spoonbill.text: As you draw face-up cards, they are not immediately refilled. Instead, wait until the end of your turn before refilling empty spaces on the bird tray. \textbf{Royal Spoonbill} allows you to reset (discard all cards on the tray and refill it) or refill the tray before drawing.
20220411@Royal Spoonbill.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250609@Australian Ibis.text: The bird card display is refilled at the end of each player's turn, including the final turn of a round, so it is refilled after a turn using \textbf{Australian Ibis}. The round-end steps then completely refresh the card row.
20250609@Australian Ibis.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220430@Australian Ibis.text: Discarded bird cards and bonus cards are discarded face up, including the card discarded when using \textbf{Australian Ibis}'s power.
20220430@Australian Ibis.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220528@Parrot Crossbill.text: When activating \textbf{Parrot Crossbill}, if all dice in the birdfeeder show the same face you may first refill the birdfeeder by rolling all dice, even though the [seed] is gained from the supply rather than from the die you remove.
20220528@Parrot Crossbill.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220804@Red-Crowned Crane.text: A bonus card discarded to score \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane} goes to the discarded bonus card pile and may be retrieved later with \textbf{Wrybill}, allowing the same bonus card to be scored twice.
20220804@Red-Crowned Crane.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230226a@Red-Crowned Crane.text: A bonus card discarded via \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane} cannot be scored at game end, so \textbf{Great Indian Bustard}'s instruction to ``also score it normally at game end'' no longer applies to that bonus card.
20230226a@Red-Crowned Crane.author: Joe Aubrey

20240120@Red-Crowned Crane.text: \textbf{Great Indian Bustard}'s ``Also score it normally at game end'' only clarifies that scoring the bonus card immediately does not prevent scoring it again at game end; you score it at game end only if you still have that bonus card. If you later discard that same bonus card (for example with \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane}), you do not score it at game end.
20240120@Red-Crowned Crane.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221226@Red-Crowned Crane.text: When scoring a bonus card immediately with \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane}, ignore any ``at game end'' wording on the bonus card and score it based on the current game state. For \textbf{Winter Feeder}, score based on the food currently in your personal supply.
20221226@Red-Crowned Crane.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220814@Behaviorist.text: For \textbf{Behaviorist}, a column is a straight stack of card slots within a single row position across the three habitats. The birds with 3 different power colors must all be in the same column; colors matched diagonally or in other arrangements do not count.
20220814@Behaviorist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220824@Masked Lapwing.text: When using \textbf{Masked Lapwing}'s power, a die showing two food types (such as a [nectar] face) counts as both types: gain 1 of each type shown, up to a maximum of 1 of each type overall.
20220824@Masked Lapwing.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260206@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} does not count for bonus cards that reward birds letting you score or draw bonus cards (such as \textbf{Endangered Species Protector}), even if the power it copied did so. Only the abilities printed on the card matter during bonus scoring.
20260206@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251108@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.text: Resolve the copied ``When Played'' power as if its text replaced \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}'s own: it applies to your board, not your neighbor's. Copying \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} therefore scores one of your own bonus cards, caching [seed] on \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}.
20251108@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250514@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} copies only the ``When Played'' power, not the copied bird's food cost, and the power only does what it can do for the copying bird: copying \textbf{Eastern Imperial Eagle} or \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} does nothing, because \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} has no [rodent] in its own cost.
20250514@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.author: Joe Aubrey

20230516@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.text: The copied power lasts for that turn only; at the end of the turn \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} no longer has it, so a copied bonus-card power does not make it count toward the \textbf{Endangered Species} bonus card at game end. Copying \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} or \textbf{Eastern Imperial Eagle} does nothing, since those powers refer to [rodent] in the bird's cost and \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} costs no [rodent].
20230516@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.author: Joe Aubrey

20221005@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.text: A ``neighbor'' in Wingspan is the players to your immediate left and right, not all players at the table.
20221005@Rose-Ringed Parakeet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221101@Sri Lanka Blue-Magpie.text: The [wild] (``any food'') symbol always includes [nectar], so you may cache [nectar] with this bird's power if you still have [nectar] in your supply when the round-end power activates.
20221101@Sri Lanka Blue-Magpie.author: Joe Aubrey

20230107@Great Cormorant.text: For powers that roll ``any'' dice you may roll dice from inside the birdfeeder, outside it, or a mix; dice taken from the birdfeeder stay out of it after rolling, until the birdfeeder is refilled.
20230107@Great Cormorant.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230830@Great Cormorant.text: If there is no [fish] cached on \textbf{Great Cormorant}, ignore the first clause and go straight to rolling 2 [die]; move 1 [fish] to your supply only when one is cached there.
20230830@Great Cormorant.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221106a@Wetland Ranger.text: Tied scores do not count as ascending or descending—5 is not higher than 5—so a run of birds worth 5, 5, 3, 3, 3 points does not form an ascending or descending sequence.
20221106a@Wetland Ranger.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230615@Forest Ranger.text: The Ranger bonus cards use strict ascending/descending, so repeated point values break the series (unlike \textbf{Data Analyst}, which explicitly allows equal wingspans). With scores of 6, 5, 5, 4, 3 in [forest], \textbf{Forest Ranger} scores only the longest strictly ascending or descending series: 5, 4, 3.
20230615@Forest Ranger.author: Joe Aubrey

20221228a@Forest Ranger.text: Tied scores do not count as ascending or descending - 5 is not higher than 5 - so scores of 1-2-2-3-5 in [forest] count as a sequence of three, not five, and a run of 5, 5, 3, 3, 3 forms no sequence at all.
20221228a@Forest Ranger.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221106a@Grassland Ranger.text: Tied scores do not count as ascending or descending—5 is not higher than 5—so a run of birds worth 5, 5, 3, 3, 3 points does not form an ascending or descending sequence.
20221106a@Grassland Ranger.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221109@Sri Lanka Frogmouth.text: The second sentence of \textbf{Sri Lanka Frogmouth}'s power is not dependent on the first: all players may discard 1 [card] to gain 1 [invertebrate] regardless of whether the die roll succeeded.
20221109@Sri Lanka Frogmouth.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230412@Hermit Thrush.text: Zero counts as ``fewest'': player(s) with no birds in their [forest] gain 1 [die] from the birdfeeder.
20230412@Hermit Thrush.author: Joe Aubrey

20221112@Hermit Thrush.text: You may decline to activate \textbf{Hermit Thrush}, but if you do activate it, the player(s) with the fewest birds in their [forest] gain their [die] - activating a power is optional, but the whole power then resolves.
20221112@Hermit Thrush.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221111@Eurasian Kestrel.text: When a power tells you to roll ``any'' dice, you choose where those dice come from (birdfeeder or table). The dice you roll are placed on the table.
20221111@Eurasian Kestrel.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221121@Brolga.text: With \textbf{Brolga}, the chosen player may decline to lay the [egg], and you still draw 2 [card] either way.
20221121@Brolga.author: Joe Aubrey

20221123@Indian Peafowl.text: Unless a power specifies that cards must be drawn from the deck or from the bird tray, you may choose where to draw each [card] from: the face-up cards in the bird tray or the top of the deck. On \textbf{Indian Peafowl}, the additional [card] you draw may come from either source, even though the first 2 [card] must come from the deck.
20221123@Indian Peafowl.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221125@Plumbeous Redstart.text: The other players keep the [card] they drew only if that card has a [invertebrate] or [seed] in its food cost; it is not the card you drew that determines this. Despite the different wording, the power works the same way as \textbf{Little Egret}.
20221125@Plumbeous Redstart.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221207@Plumbeous Redstart.text: The other players must reveal the [card] they draw, to prove whether it has a [invertebrate] or [seed] in its food cost.
20221207@Plumbeous Redstart.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221125@Little Egret.text: With \textbf{Plumbeous Redstart}, the other players keep the [card] they drew only if that card has a [invertebrate] or [seed] in its food cost; it is not the card you drew that determines this. Despite the different wording, the power works the same way as \textbf{Little Egret}.
20221125@Little Egret.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250225@Spoon-Billed Sandpiper.text: If \textbf{Spoon-Billed Sandpiper} is played at game end (for instance via a yellow power that lets you play a bird then), its power is still followed in full, including the portion letting other players discard any 2 resources to draw 2 new bonus cards and keep 1.
20250225@Spoon-Billed Sandpiper.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221210@Spoon-Billed Sandpiper.text: The 2 resources other players discard must come from their personal supply; cached food on birds may not be discarded for this.
20221210@Spoon-Billed Sandpiper.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221216@Forest Owlet.text: Dice chosen for this power are rolled outside the birdfeeder. If choosing them empties the birdfeeder, all 5 [die] are rerolled into the birdfeeder (resetting it) once the rolling is complete, before play continues.
20221216@Forest Owlet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230107@Forest Owlet.text: Where a power says to roll ``any'' dice, you may choose whether the dice come from the birdfeeder or from outside it. Either way, dice rolled for a bird power stay out of the birdfeeder.
20230107@Forest Owlet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221224@Red-Bellied Woodpecker.text: Because caching is optional, you may instead add the [seed] gained with \textbf{Red-Bellied Woodpecker}'s power to your personal food supply.
20221224@Red-Bellied Woodpecker.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250524@Winter Feeder.text: [seed] cached on \textbf{Coal Tit} or \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch} is not in your supply, so it does not count toward \textbf{Winter Feeder} even though you may spend it at any time.
20250524@Winter Feeder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221226@Winter Feeder.text: When scoring this bonus card immediately with \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane}, ignore the ``at game end'' wording and score based on the food currently in your personal supply.
20221226@Winter Feeder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250201@Winter Feeder.text: \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} can score bonus cards that specify ``at end of game'' or ``at game end,'' such as \textbf{Visionary Leader} and \textbf{Winter Feeder}, when its power is used mid-game.
20250201@Winter Feeder.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231212@Small Minivet.text: A duet token placed in the reset box of the Asia goal mat cannot be removed to reset the bird tray or the birdfeeder on the same turn it was placed; only on a later turn. Duet tokens are placed between steps 5 and 6 of your turn, so a bird that lets you play an additional bird (e.g. \textbf{Small Minivet}) does not allow you to spend a token placed earlier in that same turn.
20231212@Small Minivet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221226a@Small Minivet.text: Only the food types named on \textbf{Small Minivet} itself may be ignored in the cost of the additional bird - the printed text takes precedence over the general wording in the appendix.
20221226a@Small Minivet.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221226a@Trumpeter Finch.text: The text printed on \textbf{Small Minivet} and \textbf{Trumpeter Finch} takes precedence over the general wording in the appendix: only the food types named on the bird itself may be ignored in the cost of the additional bird.
20221226a@Trumpeter Finch.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221230@Violet Cuckoo.text: This bird's power may be used to lay an [egg] on a bird with an egg limit of 0, since it allows going 2 over the egg limit.
20221230@Violet Cuckoo.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230107@Desert Wheatear.text: Where a power says to roll ``any'' dice, you may choose whether the dice come from the birdfeeder or from outside it. Either way, dice rolled for a bird power stay out of the birdfeeder.
20230107@Desert Wheatear.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240909@Desert Wheatear.text: \textbf{Desert Wheatear} counts toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card (``ear'').
20240909@Desert Wheatear.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240120@Great Indian Bustard.text: ``Also score it normally at game end'' only clarifies that scoring the bonus card now does not prevent scoring it again at game end; you score it at game end only if you still hold that bonus card. Discard it later (for example with \textbf{Red-Crowned Crane}) and you score nothing at game end.
20240120@Great Indian Bustard.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251108@Great Indian Bustard.text: When \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} copies a neighbor's ``When Played'' power, resolve it as if the copied text replaced \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}'s own text: it applies to your board, not your neighbor's. Copying \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} therefore scores one of your own bonus cards, caching [seed] on \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet}.
20251108@Great Indian Bustard.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250201@Great Indian Bustard.text: \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} can score bonus cards that specify ``at end of game'' or ``at game end,'' such as \textbf{Visionary Leader} and \textbf{Winter Feeder}, when its power is used mid-game.
20250201@Great Indian Bustard.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230125@Great Indian Bustard.text: Cache [seed] equal to the bonus card's value when the Bustard is played (each cached [seed] is worth 1 point), then score the same bonus card again at game end for its condition at that time. Example: \textbf{Visionary Leader} with 6 [card] in hand caches 4 [seed]; at game end score \textbf{Visionary Leader} for the [card] then in hand.
20230125@Great Indian Bustard.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250201@Visionary Leader.text: \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} can score bonus cards that specify ``at end of game'' or ``at game end,'' such as \textbf{Visionary Leader} and \textbf{Winter Feeder}, when its power is used mid-game.
20250201@Visionary Leader.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230219@Visionary Leader.text: Birds in hand that score for \textbf{Visionary Leader} do not count for \textbf{Endangered Species}, which counts only birds played on your player mat; cards referring to bird cards look only at played birds unless stated otherwise.
20230219@Visionary Leader.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230125@Visionary Leader.text: \textbf{Great Indian Bustard} caches [seed] equal to \textbf{Visionary Leader}'s value when the Bustard is played (each [seed] is worth 1 point), and \textbf{Visionary Leader} is also scored normally at game end. Example: 6 [card] in hand when the Bustard is played caches 4 [seed]; at game end score for the [card] then in hand.
20230125@Visionary Leader.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231204@Wilson's Storm Petrel.text: The [card] drawn with \textbf{Wilson's Storm Petrel} are kept separate from your hand and from the other [card] you draw, and cannot be spent during this turn: they may not be played or tucked before the end of your turn, when you keep 1 of them and discard the rest (Appendix).
20231204@Wilson's Storm Petrel.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231119a@Common Tailorbird.text: Eggs laid by \textbf{Common Tailorbird}'s end-of-game power do not count toward the round 4 end-of-round goal, because that goal is scored before game-end powers are activated. See the reference tile for the order of operations.
20231119a@Common Tailorbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231119@Common Tailorbird.text: For \textbf{Common Tailorbird}, ``contiguous'' means orthogonally adjacent: directly to the left, right, above, or below, never diagonal. The group may zig-zag across rows and columns as long as each bird in the group is orthogonally adjacent to at least one other bird in the group.
20231119@Common Tailorbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230316@Blue Rock-Thrush.text: Duet tokens are only placed when you play a bird, so no one places a duet token when \textbf{Blue Rock-Thrush} or \textbf{Spotted Dove} moves to another player's mat. If a bird is later played on that space, a duet token is placed as normal.
20230316@Blue Rock-Thrush.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240111@Spotted Dove.text: When \textbf{Spotted Dove} moves to another player's mat, any cached food, [egg], or tucked [card] on it are discarded (Wingspan Asia appendix, p. 9).
20240111@Spotted Dove.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230316@Spotted Dove.text: No duet token is placed when \textbf{Spotted Dove} moves to another player's mat, since duet tokens are only placed when you play a bird. If a bird is later played on that space, a duet token is placed as normal.
20230316@Spotted Dove.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230514@Large-Billed Crow.text: When \textbf{Large-Billed Crow} caches [nectar], place it on the bird, not in your personal supply of spent [nectar].
20230514@Large-Billed Crow.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230529@Baya Weaver.text: \textbf{Baya Weaver} does not count toward the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card. That card looks for colors as words or as part of compound words, and ``Baya'' is its own word, not a compound of ``bay'' and ``a''.
20230529@Baya Weaver.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230722@Mistletoebird.text: \textbf{Spangled Drongo}'s power triggers when another player gains [nectar] in any way, including gaining [nectar] from the supply by discarding [fruit] with \textbf{Mistletoebird}'s power.
20230722@Mistletoebird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231112@Willie-Wagtail.text: \textbf{Willie-Wagtail}: you may reset the card tray only once per activation of this power. If no [card] with a [bowl] or [star] nest is available after that reset, you gain no card.
20231112@Willie-Wagtail.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240105@Blue-Winged Warbler.text: \textbf{Blue-Winged Warbler} may be played in either the [forest] or the [grassland].
20240105@Blue-Winged Warbler.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240219@Silvereye.text: For bonus cards that count birds with a color in their name, the color may be part of a compound word rather than a word of its own: \textbf{Silvereye} counts. (A letter sequence that is not a color word in the compound does not count---see \textbf{Barred Owl} and \textbf{Baya Weaver}.)
20240219@Silvereye.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240526@Wood Stork.text: ``Wood'' (singular) in a bird's name is not a geography term for the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, so birds such as \textbf{Wood Stork} and woodswallows do not count.
20240526@Wood Stork.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250619@Gray Wagtail.text: The 2 [wild] gained with \textbf{Gray Wagtail}'s round-end power may be taken as [nectar], but round-end powers resolve before unused [nectar] is discarded, so that [nectar] is immediately lost.
20250619@Gray Wagtail.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240706@Willow Tit.text: The food cached by \textbf{Willow Tit} comes from the birdfeeder, so the corresponding die must be removed from the birdfeeder. If the birdfeeder contains no [invertebrate], [seed], or [fruit], nothing is cached.
20240706@Willow Tit.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240714@Eurasian Hoopoe.text: Your neighbors are only the players directly to your right and left — at most 2 players, regardless of the number of players in the game.
20240714@Eurasian Hoopoe.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231204@Great Crested Grebe.text: The [card] drawn with \textbf{Great Crested Grebe} are kept separate from your hand and from the other [card] you draw, and cannot be spent during this turn: they may not be played or tucked before the end of your turn, when you keep 1 of them and discard the rest (Appendix).
20231204@Great Crested Grebe.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240903@Great Crested Grebe.text: The [card] drawn with \textbf{Great Crested Grebe} are kept separate from your hand until the end of your turn, when you keep 1 of them and discard the rest. Contrast \textbf{Forster's Tern}, whose drawn [card] goes into your hand, so there is nothing to discard if you have used your whole hand.
20240903@Great Crested Grebe.author: Joe Aubrey

20241104@Red Junglefowl.text: \textbf{Red Junglefowl} counts toward the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card, since ``jungle'' appears in its name.
20241104@Red Junglefowl.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20241206@European Turtle Dove.text: With \textbf{European Turtle Dove}, first draw 1 new bonus card, then choose exactly one of the three benefits: gain 1 [die] from the birdfeeder, lay 1 [egg] on any bird, or draw 1 [card].
20241206@European Turtle Dove.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20241222@Red-Tailed Hawk.text: \textbf{Red-Tailed Hawk} draws from the top of the deck, not from the 3 face-up cards on the bird tray, so its power can always be activated — there will always be cards in the deck.
20241222@Red-Tailed Hawk.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250113@Greater Adjutant.text: You must score all of your bonus cards at the end of the game (even if you earn 0 [star] from them), so you cannot decline to score a bonus card because an opponent copied it with \textbf{Greater Adjutant} or \textbf{Indian Vulture} and would score more from it than you.
20250113@Greater Adjutant.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250912@Greater Adjutant.text: When the order of Game End powers matters, activate them in clockwise order starting with the player who has the first-player token.
20250912@Greater Adjutant.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250113@Indian Vulture.text: You must score all of your bonus cards at the end of the game (even if you earn 0 [star] from them), so you cannot decline to score a bonus card because an opponent copied it with \textbf{Greater Adjutant} or \textbf{Indian Vulture} and would score more from it than you.
20250113@Indian Vulture.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250912@Indian Vulture.text: When the order of Game End powers matters, activate them in clockwise order starting with the player who has the first-player token.
20250912@Indian Vulture.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250319@Common Myna.text: \textbf{Common Myna}'s habitat restriction applies only to where it can be played, not to where it can move. If it copies a power that moves a bird to another habitat, such as \textbf{Blue Grosbeak}'s, \textbf{Common Myna} may move out of the [grassland].
20250319@Common Myna.author: Joe Aubrey

20260628@Common Myna.text: Copying a power places the other bird's power on \textbf{Common Myna} on your own player mat. If you copy a power that itself copies ``a power of a bird in the [grassland] of the player on your left'', you must still copy from another player's [grassland], not your own.
20260628@Common Myna.author: Joe Aubrey

20250401@Food Web Expert.text: \textbf{Food Web Expert} counts only birds whose food cost is [invertebrate] and nothing else. A bird with any other food symbol in its cost, even as an alternative, counts for 0. The appendix reads: ``Count the number of birds that have [invertebrate] in their food cost and no other symbols.''
20250401@Food Web Expert.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250410@Hawfinch.text: When gaining food from the birdfeeder with \textbf{Hawfinch} or \textbf{European Honey Buzzard} after resetting it, dice showing the [invertebrate]/[seed] face count: \textbf{Hawfinch} may take the [seed] from such a die, and \textbf{European Honey Buzzard} gains the [invertebrate] from such a die along with all other [invertebrate] showing.
20250410@Hawfinch.author: Joe Aubrey

20250709@Crimson Chat.text: [nectar] may be discarded to pay the [wild] cost of \textbf{Crimson Chat}. The discarded [nectar] goes to the spent nectar area of your player mat.
20250709@Crimson Chat.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250709a@House Crow.text: [nectar] may be cached with \textbf{House Crow}. Cached [nectar] is placed on the bird, not in the spent nectar area of your player mat.
20250709a@House Crow.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251006@North Island Brown Kiwi.text: If you choose to use \textbf{North Island Brown Kiwi}'s power, you must follow all of its instructions; you cannot skip discarding a bonus card and still draw bonus cards.
20251006@North Island Brown Kiwi.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251105@Western Screech-Owl.text: You may not reset the birdfeeder before using \textbf{Western Screech-Owl}'s power, even if it contains only one food type, because you are not gaining food from the birdfeeder.
20251105@Western Screech-Owl.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251108a@European Serin.text: \textbf{European Serin}'s power requires discarding all food tokens from your personal supply, not just all of one food type. You must have at least 1 food to activate it.
20251108a@European Serin.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251123@Tufted Puffin.text: When using \textbf{Tufted Puffin}, roll the same set of dice all three times; dice that roll [fish] are not removed from the pool between rolls.
20251123@Tufted Puffin.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251202@Laughing Gull.text: ``Resetting the birdfeeder'' means rerolling all the dice in the birdfeeder, however it comes about, so \textbf{Laughing Gull} also triggers (once between turns) on a reroll caused by all remaining dice showing the same face or only one die being left.
20251202@Laughing Gull.author: Joe Aubrey

20251220@Laughing Gull.text: \textbf{Laughing Gull} triggers on any birdfeeder reset during another player's turn, regardless of cause -- e.g. if their ``gain food'' action empties the birdfeeder because you took the last die with \textbf{Australian Owlet-Nightjar}, that reset still activates it.
20251220@Laughing Gull.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251220@Australian Owlet-Nightjar.text: \textbf{Laughing Gull}'s power triggers whenever the birdfeeder is reset during another player's turn, regardless of which effect caused the reset. For example, if another player's ``gain food'' action empties the birdfeeder because you took the last die with \textbf{Australian Owlet-Nightjar}, the birdfeeder reset on their turn still activates \textbf{Laughing Gull}.
20251220@Australian Owlet-Nightjar.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260116@Bird Bander.text: Hummingbird cards are birds and count toward bonus cards in the ordinary way, including \textbf{Bird Bander}, \textbf{Ecologist}, \textbf{Ethologist}, \textbf{Passerine Specialist}, \textbf{Small Clutch Specialist}, and the Data Analyst and Ranger bonus cards.
20260116@Bird Bander.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260116@Passerine Specialist.text: Hummingbird cards are birds and count toward bonus cards in the ordinary way, including \textbf{Bird Bander}, \textbf{Ecologist}, \textbf{Ethologist}, \textbf{Passerine Specialist}, \textbf{Small Clutch Specialist}, and the Data Analyst and Ranger bonus cards.
20260116@Passerine Specialist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260116@Small Clutch Specialist.text: Hummingbird cards are birds and count toward bonus cards in the ordinary way, including \textbf{Bird Bander}, \textbf{Ecologist}, \textbf{Ethologist}, \textbf{Passerine Specialist}, \textbf{Small Clutch Specialist}, and the Data Analyst and Ranger bonus cards.
20260116@Small Clutch Specialist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260124@Yellow-Eyed Penguin.text: A bird played for free with \textbf{Yellow-Eyed Penguin} still triggers its ``when played'' power, but powers that refer to a paid cost have no effect: \textbf{Bonelli's Eagle} tucks no [card] when played for free.
20260124@Yellow-Eyed Penguin.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260728@Yellow-Eyed Penguin.text: A bird played using a ``game end'' (yellow) power such as \textbf{Yellow-Eyed Penguin} still gives you its ``when played'' (white) and ``game end'' (yellow) powers, even if the yellow power does not say so; \textbf{Gould's Finch} and \textbf{Grey-Headed Mannikin} state this only for extra clarity.
20260728@Yellow-Eyed Penguin.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260128@Ivory Gull.text: Food cached on \textbf{Ivory Gull} may only be spent on the cost of a bird power, not to play a bird -- including a bird played via another bird's power, such as \textbf{Tufted Titmouse}.
20260128@Ivory Gull.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260210@Ivory Gull.text: Food cached on \textbf{Ivory Gull} may be spent just like food in your personal supply whenever a bird power asks you to pay food to do something.
20260210@Ivory Gull.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260208@Great Kiskadee.text: \textbf{Great Kiskadee} and \textbf{Tropical Kingbird}: After moving with the action cube, continue activating birds only in the new habitat---you do not activate the core action of the new habitat.
20260208@Great Kiskadee.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260208b@Great Kiskadee.text: For pink ``once between turns'' powers that trigger on another player taking a specific core action, the action that counts is the one taken where the cube started, since the core action happens at the beginning of the turn---not the core action of the habitat this bird moves to.
20260208b@Great Kiskadee.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260208@Tropical Kingbird.text: \textbf{Great Kiskadee} and \textbf{Tropical Kingbird}: After moving with the action cube, continue activating birds only in the new habitat---you do not activate the core action of the new habitat.
20260208@Tropical Kingbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260208b@Tropical Kingbird.text: For pink ``once between turns'' powers that trigger on another player taking a specific core action, the action that counts is the one taken where the cube started, since the core action happens at the beginning of the turn---not the core action of the habitat this bird moves to.
20260208b@Tropical Kingbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260206@Endangered Species Protector.text: \textbf{Rose-Ringed Parakeet} does not count toward the \textbf{Endangered Species Protector} bonus card even if it was used to copy a ``When Played'' power that scored or drew bonus cards. Only the abilities printed on the card matter during bonus scoring.
20260206@Endangered Species Protector.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260208a@Altamira Oriole.text: When this bird's power attracts a hummingbird, you activate that hummingbird card's benefit.
20260208a@Altamira Oriole.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260209@Great Eared Nightjar.text: \textbf{Great Eared Nightjar}'s power looks for the [forest] icon printed on the drawn bird cards. Any bird with a [forest] icon counts, even if it also has other habitat icons.
20260209@Great Eared Nightjar.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260209a@Blue-and-Yellow Macaw.text: When \textbf{Blue-and-Yellow Macaw} attracts a hummingbird, it may be placed in any hummingbird slot, not only one in the [forest]. Card abilities that attract or return hummingbirds are not limited to the habitat the bird is in.
20260209a@Blue-and-Yellow Macaw.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260313@Rufous Hornero.text: The eggs placed by \textbf{Rufous Hornero} are placeholders: they do not count as eggs in your preserve for any other purpose, so they do not count toward end-of-round goals or end-of-game scoring. Those spaces are still empty for powers that count empty spaces.
20260313@Rufous Hornero.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260211@Rufous Hornero.text: An [egg] placed by this power can only help pay the egg cost of the bird played on top of it; it cannot be spent on a bird in another habitat or slot. If that bird needs no eggs (column 1), discard the egg.
20260211@Rufous Hornero.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260213@Muscovy Duck.text: This power only attracts hummingbirds; it does not let you return hummingbirds already on your player mat. You may attract only as many as you have open hummingbird spaces (1 or 2), and if all your hummingbird spaces are full you attract none. Nectar shown on an attracted hummingbird is gained as normal, even though this is a round end power.
20260213@Muscovy Duck.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260213a@Bat Falcon.text: Standard tucking rules apply to the hummingbird tucked behind this bird.
20260213a@Bat Falcon.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260214@Southern Lapwing.text: \textbf{Southern Lapwing}'s power is an independent choice ([egg] or [card]) for each empty slot in your [forest], so you may mix the two: with 5 empty slots you could lay 3 [egg] and draw 2 [card].
20260214@Southern Lapwing.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260217@California Scrub-Jay.text: \textbf{California Scrub-Jay}: ``Upgrading an action'' refers to the optional portion of the core action benefits printed on the player mat. Any time another player pays for and uses such an upgraded benefit -- including the choice between multiple upgrade options in a habitat, such as rerolling the birdfeeder or gaining an extra food -- it counts for this bird.
20260217@California Scrub-Jay.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260226@Titicaca Grebe.text: When using \textbf{Titicaca Grebe}'s power, the drawn bonus cards are looked at, not chosen blindly: you look at them and choose 1, then the next player looks at the remaining cards and chooses 1, and so on.
20260226@Titicaca Grebe.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260305@Blue-Headed Parrot.text: If the card drawn with \textbf{Blue-Headed Parrot}'s power has both [seed] and [fruit] in its food cost, you still gain only 1 food token from the supply; choose which one.
20260305@Blue-Headed Parrot.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260510@Lineated Woodpecker.text: For powers that check which action types you used this round, such as \textbf{White Wagtail}, look at where each action cube ended up, as that is the game's way of remembering. A bird such as \textbf{Lineated Woodpecker} that moves with the action cube to another habitat therefore changes which action the cube records.
20260510@Lineated Woodpecker.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260307@Lineated Woodpecker.text: After \textbf{Lineated Woodpecker} moves with the action cube and you continue your turn in the new habitat, you activate only the brown powers in the habitat where the cube now is; you do not activate the remaining powers of the habitat it left.
20260307@Lineated Woodpecker.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260208b@Lineated Woodpecker.text: For pink ``once between turns'' powers that trigger on another player taking a specific core action, the action that counts is the one taken where the cube started, since the core action happens at the beginning of the turn---not the core action of the habitat this bird moves to.
20260208b@Lineated Woodpecker.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260324@Garden Warbler.text: With \textbf{Garden Warbler}, the additional bird is played first and completely, including its own ``when played'' power, and only then is 1 [egg] laid on both birds. If the additional bird is \textbf{Red Kite} (or a similar bird) played on top of \textbf{Garden Warbler}, turning \textbf{Garden Warbler} into a tucked card, the egg laying still takes place.
20260324@Garden Warbler.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260604@Canada Jay.text: \textbf{Canada Jay}: you may cache 1 [wild] from your personal supply and then immediately gain 1 food of that same type from the general supply in the same activation.
20260604@Canada Jay.author: Joe Aubrey

20260713@Crested Oropendola.text: Hummingbird bonuses are only triggered when a hummingbird marker moves up the track, so moving a marker down with \textbf{Crested Oropendola} does not trigger the bonus of the space it lands on. To trigger a bonus again you must move down twice and then up at least once; an infinite loop is not possible.
20260713@Crested Oropendola.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260712@Orinoco Goose.text: For \textbf{Orinoco Goose}, adjacent [star] nest birds count as [cavity] birds.
20260712@Orinoco Goose.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260728@Dovekie.text: When a bird is played using a ``game end'' (yellow) power such as \textbf{Dovekie} or \textbf{Yellow-Eyed Penguin}, you still gain the benefits of its ``when played'' (white) and ``game end'' (yellow) powers, even if the yellow power does not say so. \textbf{Gould's Finch} and \textbf{Grey-Headed Mannikin} state this explicitly only for extra clarity.
20260728@Dovekie.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260731@Red-Legged Seriema.text: \textbf{Red-Legged Seriema}'s power looks at the birdfeeder after a single reset, checking simultaneously for [seed] and [rodent]. You may not claim some of those tokens and then reset the birdfeeder again to gain more.
20260731@Red-Legged Seriema.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260812@Hummingbird Counter.text: Score 1 point for each [hummingbird] space on your hummingbird track that you have reached or exceeded.
20260812@Hummingbird Counter.author: Joe Aubrey

20260818@Red-Headed Woodpecker.text: ``May'' creates a choice. On \textbf{Red-Headed Woodpecker}, you may decline to cache the [seed] and instead keep it as a normal food resource to spend later.
20260818@Red-Headed Woodpecker.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200401@Eurasian Green Woodpecker.text: A goal such as ``birds with [cavity] nests with at least 1 [egg]'' counts birds, so \textbf{Eurasian Green Woodpecker} counts as two of them once it has an [egg] on it. The [egg] themselves are never doubled: the \textit{European Expansion} rulebook's OTHER POWERS section states that eggs on these cards are not doubled if the goal is counting eggs.
20200401@Eurasian Green Woodpecker.author: Joe Aubrey

20200405b@Cetti's Warbler.text: ``Sets of [egg]'' counts eggs and ``food cost of birds'' counts food, so \textbf{Cetti's Warbler} does not count double toward either. For a goal it qualifies for that counts birds, such as ``birds in [wetland]'', it counts as two birds.
20200405b@Cetti's Warbler.author: Joe Aubrey

20210123@Greylag Goose.text: ``Birds in one row'' and ``[ground] nest birds with [egg]'' both count birds, so \textbf{Greylag Goose} counts double toward each. ``[egg] in [wetland]'' counts eggs, not birds, so it does not.
20210123@Greylag Goose.author: Joe Aubrey

20220914@Cetti's Warbler.text: ``Filled columns'' counts columns rather than birds, so this bird does not let you count an extra filled column; it counts only in the column it occupies.
20220914@Cetti's Warbler.author: Joe Aubrey

20220914@Eurasian Green Woodpecker.text: ``Filled columns'' counts columns rather than birds, so this bird does not let you count an extra filled column; it counts only in the column it occupies.
20220914@Eurasian Green Woodpecker.author: Joe Aubrey

20220914@Greylag Goose.text: ``Filled columns'' counts columns rather than birds, so this bird does not let you count an extra filled column; it counts only in the column it occupies.
20220914@Greylag Goose.author: Joe Aubrey

20200218@Grey Heron.text: A bird played on top of \textbf{Grey Heron} also goes sideways and covers \textbf{Grey Heron} completely, which becomes a tucked card.
20200218@Grey Heron.author: Joe Aubrey

20200218@Red Kite.text: When \textbf{Red Kite} is played on top of a sideways bird such as \textbf{Grey Heron}, it also goes sideways and covers that bird completely, which becomes a tucked card.
20200218@Red Kite.author: Joe Aubrey

20260716@Western Yellow Wagtail.text: Bird powers only take effect once the bird has been played, so \textbf{Western Yellow Wagtail} does not count double for \textbf{Visionary Leader} if you leave it in your hand. For \textbf{Ecologist}, counting it twice does raise the number of birds in its habitat, so if the habitats otherwise hold equal numbers of birds, its habitat is no longer the one with the fewest.
20260716@Western Yellow Wagtail.author: Joe Aubrey

20260716@Visionary Leader.text: Bird powers only take effect once the bird has been played, so \textbf{Western Yellow Wagtail} does not count double for \textbf{Visionary Leader} if you leave it in your hand. For \textbf{Ecologist}, counting it twice does raise the number of birds in its habitat, so if the habitats otherwise hold equal numbers of birds, its habitat is no longer the one with the fewest.
20260716@Visionary Leader.author: Joe Aubrey

20260716@Ecologist.text: Bird powers only take effect once the bird has been played, so \textbf{Western Yellow Wagtail} does not count double for \textbf{Visionary Leader} if you leave it in your hand. For \textbf{Ecologist}, counting it twice does raise the number of birds in its habitat, so if the habitats otherwise hold equal numbers of birds, its habitat is no longer the one with the fewest.
20260716@Ecologist.author: Joe Aubrey

20201206b@Chimney Swift.text: Habitat restrictions apply only when a bird is played. Afterwards a power such as \textbf{Chimney Swift}'s---including when it is copied by \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} or \textbf{Tūī}---may move a bird into a habitat where it could not have been played.
20201206b@Chimney Swift.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210701@Anatomist.text: A single bird may count toward more than one bonus card. These bonus cards never look at scientific (Latin) names, and other language editions handle them differently, so check the rulebook of the edition you are playing.
20210701@Anatomist.author: Joe Aubrey

20210701@Cartographer.text: A single bird may count toward more than one bonus card. These bonus cards never look at scientific (Latin) names, and other language editions handle them differently, so check the rulebook of the edition you are playing.
20210701@Cartographer.author: Joe Aubrey

20210701@Photographer.text: A single bird may count toward more than one bonus card. These bonus cards never look at scientific (Latin) names, and other language editions handle them differently, so check the rulebook of the edition you are playing.
20210701@Photographer.author: Joe Aubrey

20210920@Round end.text: Teal ROUND END powers trigger at the end of every round after the bird is played, not only the round in which it was played, so a bird played in round 1 may activate its round end power up to 4 times.
20210920@Round end.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231030@Black Vulture.text: When more than one player's ``once between turns'' power is triggered at the same time, they resolve in turn order starting with the player after the active player. \textbf{Black Vulture}, \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie} and \textbf{Turkey Vulture} are all triggered and activated as soon as the successful [predator] finishes its power, before the active player continues to their next bird.
20231030@Black Vulture.author: Joe Aubrey

20231030@Black-Billed Magpie.text: When more than one player's ``once between turns'' power is triggered at the same time, they resolve in turn order starting with the player after the active player. \textbf{Black Vulture}, \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie} and \textbf{Turkey Vulture} are all triggered and activated as soon as the successful [predator] finishes its power, before the active player continues to their next bird.
20231030@Black-Billed Magpie.author: Joe Aubrey

20231030@Turkey Vulture.text: When more than one player's ``once between turns'' power is triggered at the same time, they resolve in turn order starting with the player after the active player. \textbf{Black Vulture}, \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie} and \textbf{Turkey Vulture} are all triggered and activated as soon as the successful [predator] finishes its power, before the active player continues to their next bird.
20231030@Turkey Vulture.author: Joe Aubrey

20240115@Black-Billed Magpie.text: When a power is copied, the whole power including its label transfers to the copying bird. A bird such as \textbf{Tūī} that copies a [predator] power therefore has a [predator] power while it activates it, and its success triggers \textbf{Black-Billed Magpie}.
20240115@Black-Billed Magpie.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201010b@Eurasian Nuthatch.text: The ``at any time'' in this power covers paying a cost in another bird's power: a [seed] cached on \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch} may be spent to discard for \textbf{Sandhill Crane}'s tuck.
20201010b@Eurasian Nuthatch.author: Joe Aubrey

20201010b@Sandhill Crane.text: Cached food normally cannot be spent, but \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch}'s ``at any time'' overrides that: a [seed] cached on it may be discarded to pay this power's cost.
20201010b@Sandhill Crane.author: Joe Aubrey

20201010b@Black-Bellied Whistling-Duck.text: Cached food normally cannot be spent, but \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch}'s ``at any time'' overrides that: a [seed] cached on it may be discarded to pay this power's cost.
20201010b@Black-Bellied Whistling-Duck.author: Joe Aubrey

20201010b@Canada Goose.text: Cached food normally cannot be spent, but \textbf{Eurasian Nuthatch}'s ``at any time'' overrides that: a [seed] cached on it may be discarded to pay this power's cost.
20201010b@Canada Goose.author: Joe Aubrey

02c@Lesser Prairie-Chicken.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card: \textit{prairie} is a qualifying keyword. (Early printings of that bonus card did not list it; the omission was corrected in print by December 2019.)

02c@Prairie Falcon.text: This bird counts toward the \textbf{Cartographer} bonus card: \textit{prairie} is a qualifying keyword. (Early printings of that bonus card did not list it; the omission was corrected in print by December 2019.)

20191203c@Violet Cuckoo.text: \textit{Violet} is a qualifying keyword for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card, so \textbf{Violet Cuckoo} counts toward it.

20191203c@Violet-Green Swallow.text: \textit{Violet} is a qualifying keyword for the \textbf{Photographer} bonus card, though \textbf{Violet-Green Swallow} also contains \textit{green}, so it counts either way.

20191004@Round end powers.text: Each player chooses the order in which they activate their own round end (teal) powers.
20191004@Round end powers.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250928@Black-Tailed Godwit.text: Activating this power commits you to all of it: you may not decline the new bonus card after seeing it, and you must keep 1 of the 3 [card] you draw.
20250928@Black-Tailed Godwit.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250928@Philippine Eagle.text: If at least 3 [rodent] are showing when you stop, you must follow the power through to completion: draw 2 bonus cards and keep 1 of them, even after seeing that you would rather keep neither.
20250928@Philippine Eagle.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251210@Anatomist.text: Words that refer to a body part only figuratively do not count: the ``poll'' in \textbf{Blackpoll Warbler} and the ``start'' in redstart names are interpretations of a word rather than anatomical words. A group may agree to count them, as long as it is consistent.
20251210@Anatomist.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20251210@Blackpoll Warbler.text: \textbf{Blackpoll Warbler} does not officially count toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card: ``poll'' refers to the head only figuratively, and the card looks for anatomical words. A group may agree to count it, as long as it is consistent.
20251210@Blackpoll Warbler.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20201020b@Bushtit.text: \textbf{Bushtit} does not officially count toward the \textbf{Anatomist} bonus card, though some groups house-rule otherwise.
20201020b@Bushtit.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260109@Orange-Breasted Bunting.text: This power does not name a habitat, so you may attract or return the hummingbird in any habitat; it need not be the habitat where this bird is played.
20260109@Orange-Breasted Bunting.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260212@Great Crested Grebe.text: Empty hummingbird spaces in the row count as empty card slots for this power, so a lone bird in the first [wetland] slot with no hummingbird attracted draws 5 [card]. This was confirmed ``at least for now,'' so it may be revisited.
20260212@Great Crested Grebe.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260319@Gray Catbird.text: A ``repeat'' power makes the other bird's power trigger again on that bird itself; it is not a copy performed by this bird. If the repeated power's condition is no longer met for that bird---for example, a bird that must be the rightmost in its habitat is no longer at the right edge---the repeated power simply fizzles.
20260319@Gray Catbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260319@Northern Mockingbird.text: A ``repeat'' power makes the other bird's power trigger again on that bird itself; it is not a copy performed by this bird. If the repeated power's condition is no longer met for that bird---for example, a bird that must be the rightmost in its habitat is no longer at the right edge---the repeated power simply fizzles.
20260319@Northern Mockingbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200108@Gray Catbird.text: This bird does not take on the other bird's power; that bird repeats its own power as if it were activated again. [card] tucked by a repeated tucking power (e.g., \textbf{Barn Swallow}) go behind that bird, and any food or [egg] cost is paid as that bird's power specifies (e.g., \textbf{Chihuahuan Raven} still requires discarding 1 [egg] from one of your other birds). A bird that gains tucked [card] this way does not gain a [flocking] power, but does count toward \textbf{Citizen Scientist}.
20200108@Gray Catbird.author: Joe Aubrey

20200108@Northern Mockingbird.text: This bird does not take on the other bird's power; that bird repeats its own power as if it were activated again. [card] tucked by a repeated tucking power (e.g., \textbf{Barn Swallow}) go behind that bird, and any food or [egg] cost is paid as that bird's power specifies (e.g., \textbf{Chihuahuan Raven} still requires discarding 1 [egg] from one of your other birds). A bird that gains tucked [card] this way does not gain a [flocking] power, but does count toward \textbf{Citizen Scientist}.
20200108@Northern Mockingbird.author: Joe Aubrey

20190307@Gray Catbird.text: This bird can only repeat the power of a bird that is currently in the same habitat. If a bird has already used a ``move this bird to another habitat'' power and left, it can no longer be repeated here; repeat its power first and it may then move.
20190307@Gray Catbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190307@Northern Mockingbird.text: This bird can only repeat the power of a bird that is currently in the same habitat. If a bird has already used a ``move this bird to another habitat'' power and left, it can no longer be repeated here; repeat its power first and it may then move.
20190307@Northern Mockingbird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260713b@Great Kiskadee.text: When \textbf{Great Kiskadee}'s power is repeated by another bird (e.g., \textbf{Gray Catbird} or \textbf{Northern Mockingbird}), the action cube is not on \textbf{Great Kiskadee}, so the power has no effect.
20260713b@Great Kiskadee.author: Joe Aubrey

20260520@Wattled Jacana.text: To ``refill'' the bird tray is to place a [card] from the deck on each empty slot of the tray; this is not the same as resetting the tray.
20260520@Wattled Jacana.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260520@Red-Wattled Lapwing.text: To ``refill'' the bird tray is to place a [card] from the deck on each empty slot of the tray; this is not the same as resetting the tray.
20260520@Red-Wattled Lapwing.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200104@Common Nighthawk.text: After this bird moves, you carry on activating the habitat you originally chose---the move does not give you the benefits of the new habitat.
20200104@Common Nighthawk.author: Joe Aubrey

20200113@Blue Jay.text: The normal reroll rules apply while you look for the [seed]: if every [die] in the birdfeeder shows the same face you may reroll them all, including when only 1 [die] is left in the birdfeeder.
20200113@Blue Jay.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210417b@Superb Lyrebird.text: \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} and \textbf{Tūī} may copy each other's copying power. Doing so copies a brown power in the relevant player's [forest], which in a 2-player game can mean copying one of your own brown powers.
20210417b@Superb Lyrebird.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20210417b@Tūī.text: \textbf{Superb Lyrebird} and \textbf{Tūī} may copy each other's copying power. Doing so copies a brown power in the relevant player's [forest], which in a 2-player game can mean copying one of your own brown powers.
20210417b@Tūī.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231008@European Goldfinch.text: If the deck runs out, shuffle the discard pile to form a new deck. If no [card] are left in the game at all there is nothing to tuck, and this power cannot be used. Tucked [card] are effectively counters---nothing on the other side of a tucked card matters for play---but they are real bird cards, removed from the deck.
20231008@European Goldfinch.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260520b@End of turn.text: Powers that trigger ``at the end of your turn'' trigger after hummingbird actions, since hummingbird actions happen during your turn.
20260520b@End of turn.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260605@Resolving powers that involve a.topic: Resolving powers that involve all players
20260605@Resolving powers that involve a.text: When a bird power has each player make a selection, all players make their selections in turn order; the active player then carries on activating the remaining brown powers in that habitat until their turn ends.
20260605@Resolving powers that involve a.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260814@Laying eggs with bird powers.text: The restriction that [egg] must be laid on different birds belongs to the lay eggs action, not to bird powers. When a power lets you lay more than one [egg], you may lay them all on the same bird, up to that bird's [egg] limit.
20260814@Laying eggs with bird powers.author: Joe Aubrey

20260816@Gaining specific foods from the.topic: Gaining specific foods from the birdfeeder
20260816@Gaining specific foods from the.text: When a power tells you to gain more than one specific type of food from the birdfeeder, gain only the types actually in the birdfeeder; the food that is not there is simply not gained, and the birdfeeder is not reset or refilled to look for it.
20260816@Gaining specific foods from the.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221116@Drawn cards enter your hand.text: [card] you draw enter your hand immediately, so a [card] you have just drawn is eligible when a power tells you to discard a [card] from your hand.
20221116@Drawn cards enter your hand.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20231228@Wingspan of flightless birds.text: A bird with a [star] wingspan has no printed wingspan. Per page 3 of the \textit{Oceania} rulebook, treat its wingspan as any length you want it to be, whether for an end-of-round goal, a bonus card, or a power that looks at wingspan.
20231228@Wingspan of flightless birds.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221013@Wild wingspan.text: A [star] wingspan is wild for each bonus card separately, in the same way a [wild] nest can act as a different nest type for each bonus card, goal or power. \textbf{Emu} can count as a mid-sized wingspan for \textbf{Grassland Data Analyst} and as a wingspan over 65 cm for \textbf{Large Bird Specialist} at the same time.
20221013@Wild wingspan.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20240713@Rerolling dice.text: Unless a card says otherwise, the birdfeeder [die] are rerolled in exactly two situations: when the birdfeeder is empty of [die], refill it immediately by rolling all 5; and when a player is about to gain food and every [die] in the birdfeeder shows the same face, that player may refill it by rolling all 5. There is no default option to pay food to reset the birdfeeder.
20240713@Rerolling dice.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200413@Tucking.text: There is no limit to the number of [card] that may be tucked behind a bird.
20200413@Tucking.author: Joe Aubrey

20210830@Rolling dice outside the birdfe.text: Powers that say ``Roll all dice not in birdfeeder'' are always resolved outside of the birdfeeder: do not roll those dice back into the birdfeeder, and consider only the dice rolled outside it, not the dice sitting in the birdfeeder. If there are no dice outside the birdfeeder, the power has no dice to roll and gains nothing.
20210830@Rolling dice outside the birdfe.author: Joe Aubrey

20210830b@When Played.text: A ``When Played'' power resolves only after the bird has been played, so the bird's cost must be paid first---you cannot use \textbf{Brown Pelican}'s power to gain the [fish] needed to pay for it.
20210830b@When Played.author: Joe Aubrey

20210830c@Ties.text: When a power refers to the ``player(s) with the fewest'' something, the ``(s)'' means that if several players are tied for the fewest, they all gain the benefit.
20210830c@Ties.author: Joe Aubrey

20210830d@Laying eggs with bird powers.text: [egg] laid by a bird power must always be placed on a nest with available space; you may not hold [egg] to the side of your player mat.
20210830d@Laying eggs with bird powers.author: Joe Aubrey

20200504@Rolling dice outside the birdfe.text: When the birdfeeder becomes empty, all 5 [die] are immediately refilled and rerolled before anything else happens, so a power that rolls the dice not in the birdfeeder can roll at most 4 of them.
20200504@Rolling dice outside the birdfe.author: Joe Aubrey

20220429@Drawing cards.text: A power that says ``Look at a [card] from the deck'' must use the top card of the deck; a face-up card from the bird tray may not be used.
20220429@Drawing cards.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220429b@Drawing cards.text: A power that says ``Draw [card]'' without naming a source lets you take either a face-up [card] from the bird tray or the top [card] of the deck. (Contrast \textbf{Great Horned Owl}, whose ``Look at a [card] from the deck'' must use the top card of the deck.)
20220429b@Drawing cards.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20260503@Caching.text: A ``you may cache'' power is literal and the ``may'' is a genuine choice: food you gain goes to your personal supply, and you may instead choose to cache any or all of it on this bird, where it scores 1 point at the end of the game instead of being available to spend.
20260503@Caching.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20190617@Food cost of bird powers.text: Paying 2 food of one type in place of 1 food of another type applies only when playing a bird; it cannot pay a food cost inside a bird's power, such as discarding 1 [seed] for \textbf{Canada Goose}.
20190617@Food cost of bird powers.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220516@Nectar.text: [nectar] is not wild for a bird power that names a specific food type: \textbf{Canada Goose} requires discarding a [seed], and [nectar] may not be discarded instead. [nectar] is wild only when paying food to play a bird, using an ``any food'' bird power, or upgrading an action.
20220516@Nectar.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20220326@Powers.text: Activating a bird power is optional, including a teal (round end) or pink (once between turns) power. A player may decline to activate one---for example, to avoid laying [egg] on a bird when the end-of-round goal counts birds with no [egg].
20220326@Powers.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20230827@Powers.text: Powers that refer to types of birds (e.g., \textbf{Carrion Crow}, which caches 1 [rodent] for each [predator] a player has) always refer to birds played on a player mat, never to birds in hand.
20230827@Powers.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250928@Red Knot.text: Activating this power commits you to all of it: you may not decline the new bonus card after seeing it, and you must keep 1 of the 3 [card] you draw.
20250928@Red Knot.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20221210@Crested Ibis.text: The 2 resources other players discard must come from their personal supply; cached food on birds may not be discarded for this.
20221210@Crested Ibis.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20250225@Crested Ibis.text: If \textbf{Crested Ibis} is played at game end (for instance via a yellow power that lets you play a bird then), its power is still followed in full, including the portion letting other players discard any 2 resources to draw 2 new bonus cards and keep 1.
20250225@Crested Ibis.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20191126b@White-Backed Woodpecker.text: This bird's power lets you take 1 food from the birdfeeder, as if [wild] were replaced by [die] in the power text.

20210127@Common Nightingale.text: [nectar] counts as a food type for this bird's power, so you may choose [nectar] and all players gain 1 [nectar] from the supply.
20210127@Common Nightingale.author: Jamey Stegmaier

20200423b@Food cost of bird powers.text: The food a power tells you to discard is a cost, not something you may substitute or skip: if you cannot pay it you cannot use the power, and you may not take the benefit without paying---no [seed], no tuck for \textbf{Sandhill Crane}.
20200423b@Food cost of bird powers.author: Joe Aubrey

20221121b@Powers.text: Any player may decline a benefit, whether it comes from their own power or from another player's power. Having food stolen is not a benefit, so a player being stolen from has no choice.
20221121b@Powers.author: Joe Aubrey

Whenever you are entitled to gain resources, you may choose to take some but not all of the quantity specified.

Regular reroll rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder: whenever you go to the birdfeeder to gain food for any reason—caching included, and including a power that gains 1 [die] or that gains a specific food "if available"—you may reroll if all the [die] in the birdfeeder show the same face. A single remaining [die] trivially shows the same face, so it may be rerolled. You may also take fewer food than the birdfeeder offers and reroll before choosing the next.

Unless a card says otherwise, the birdfeeder [die] are rerolled in exactly two situations: when the birdfeeder is empty of [die], refill it immediately by rolling all 5; and when a player is about to gain food and every [die] in the birdfeeder shows the same face, that player may refill it by rolling all 5. There is no default option to pay food to reset the birdfeeder.

general_texts: Powers that say "Roll all dice not in birdfeeder" are always resolved outside of the birdfeeder: do not roll those dice back into the birdfeeder, and consider only the dice rolled outside it, not the dice sitting in the birdfeeder. When the birdfeeder becomes empty, all 5 [die] are immediately refilled and rerolled before anything else happens, so a power that rolls the dice not in the birdfeeder can roll at most 4 of them.

Powers that refer to types of birds (e.g., Carrion Crow, which caches 1 [rodent] for each [predator] a player has) always refer to birds played on a player mat, never to birds in hand.

Teal ROUND END powers trigger at the end of every round after the bird is played, not only the round in which it was played, so a bird played in round 1 may activate its round end power up to 4 times.
Each player chooses the order in which they activate their own round end (teal) powers.

Activating a bird power is optional, including a teal (round end) or pink (once between turns) power. A player may decline to activate one—for example, to avoid laying [egg] on a bird when the end-of-round goal counts birds with no [egg].

Sri Lanka Frogmouth.power: Roll any 1 [die]. If you roll a [invertebrate], cache 1 [invertebrate] from the supply on this bird. All players may discard 1 [card] from their hand to gain 1 [invertebrate] from the supply.
general_texts: When a bird power has each player make a selection, all players make their selections in turn order; the active player then carries on activating the remaining brown powers in that habitat until their turn ends.
Any player may decline a benefit, whether it comes from their own power or from another player's power. Having food stolen is not a benefit, so a player being stolen from has no choice.
You may only reroll dice when gaining food from the birdfeeder and not when gaining food from the supply.
Whenever you are entitled to gain resources, you may choose to take some but not all of the quantity specified.

general_texts: You may substitute 2 [wild] for any 1 food in a bird's food cost whenever you play a bird, including outside the scope of the "play a bird" action.

Teal ROUND END powers trigger at the end of every round after the bird is played, not only the round in which it was played, so a bird played in round 1 may activate its round end power up to 4 times.
Each player chooses the order in which they activate their own round end (teal) powers.

Activating a bird power is optional, including a teal (round end) or pink (once between turns) power. A player may decline to activate one—for example, to avoid laying [egg] on a bird when the end-of-round goal counts birds with no [egg].

Yellowhead.power: Reset the birdfeeder twice. Each time, cache all [invertebrate] rolled on this bird.

Zebra Dove.power: All players may discard 1 [seed] from their supply to lay 1 [egg].
general_texts: Paying 2 food of one type in place of 1 food of another type applies only when playing a bird; it cannot pay a food cost inside a bird's power, such as discarding 1 [seed] for Canada Goose.

[nectar] is not wild for a bird power that names a specific food type: Canada Goose requires discarding a [seed], and [nectar] may not be discarded instead. [nectar] is wild only when paying food to play a bird, using an "any food" bird power, or upgrading an action.

The food a power tells you to discard is a cost, not something you may substitute or skip: if you cannot pay it you cannot use the power, and you may not take the benefit without paying—no [seed], no tuck for Sandhill Crane.
"Discarding" food while resolving a bird power counts as "spending".

When a bird power has each player make a selection, all players make their selections in turn order; the active player then carries on activating the remaining brown powers in that habitat until their turn ends.
Any player may decline a benefit, whether it comes from their own power or from another player's power. Having food stolen is not a benefit, so a player being stolen from has no choice.
[egg] laid by a bird power must always be placed on a nest with available space; you may not hold [egg] to the side of your player mat.
